guides.summary: Use “Purist - Caster” to stack absurd Ability Haste so Maokai can endlessly toss E saplings into bushes, then pair it with “From Downtown” so saplings and your ult call down meteors every time they hit an enemy from over 700 units away, creating a long-range torture build that fills the screen with falling stars.

## Core Augments:

- ![augment:Purist - Caster](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2018.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:From Downtown](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2103.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

## Recommended Build

The first three items are locked in:

1. ![item:Blackfire Torch](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/222503.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
2. ![item:Imperial Mandate](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/324005.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
3. ![item:Malignance](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223118.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

These three mainly provide:

- Ability Power
- Ability Haste
- Damage-over-time burn
- Ultimate Ability Haste
- Bonus damage on the meteor shower after your R lands its crowd control

### If you only have Caster

If all you have is "Purist - Caster," you need to follow up with attack speed items so you keep converting attack speed into Ability Haste.

- ![item:Lich Bane](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223100.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![item:Nashor's Tooth](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223115.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The core idea is not to make Maokai auto attack, it's:

> attack speed items
> → Caster converts it into Ability Haste
> → E and R cooldowns drop even further

### If you have extra CD augments

If you've already picked up Eureka, Infinite Recursion, or other big haste sources, there's no need to force attack speed.

From there you can go straight into:

- ![item:Liandry's Torment](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/6653.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

That way both each individual sapling and each From Downtown proc hit much harder.

## Other Recommended Augments

- ![augment:Eureka](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1030.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Eureka and Infinite Recursion in particular are perfect here.

The more Ability Haste you have:

> the more E charges you get
> → the more saplings you can pre-plant in bushes
> → the more often you can cast R
> → the more times From Downtown procs

So this build doesn't want every augment going into single-hit damage — **cooldown is actually the most important stat.**

## Playstyle Summary

The core synergy of meteor shower Maokai is:

> Caster gives you enormous Ability Haste
> → endlessly pre-plant E in the bushes
> → R roots enemies from long range
> → a swarm of saplings chases them down at once
> → damage from over 700 units away procs From Downtown
> → meteor after meteor rains down

The end game isn't diving in as a tank, it's standing in the back planting trees like a lunatic:

> **Stack E in the bushes → R to lock them down → saplings detonate → screen-wide meteor shower**

guides.title: Infinite R Kayle: Archmage / Mystic Punch Dual Routes
guides.summary: There are two main ways to get infinite R Kayle online: one uses “Archmage” to have W and R refresh each other; the other uses “Mystic Punch” with a pile of on-hit effects to burn down the ult cooldown fast.
guides.gameplay:
## Route 1: Archmage CD Build

Core augments:

- ![augment:Archmage](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2087.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Purist - Caster](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2018.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

After that, add any high-haste augments:

- ![augment:Eureka](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1030.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Ultimate Awakening](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1349.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Infinite Recursion](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1388.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Shrink Engine](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1373.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Recursion](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1068.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

### How It Works

Kayle's W, Celestial Blessing, has a fixed 15 second base cooldown.

Once you have Archmage, casting W refunds cooldown to your other abilities equal to 30% of the cast ability's original cooldown:

> 15 × 30% = 4.5 seconds

So as long as you push Kayle's actual ultimate cooldown low enough, you can use W to keep refreshing R over and over.

> **Get R's actual cooldown under 7 seconds**

Once it's online, the loop is:

> R → W refreshes R → R → W → R

The ult's own duration burns off a chunk of natural cooldown, and combined with the 4.5 seconds W refunds, the next R comes back up almost immediately.

### Recommended Build

1. ![item:Malignance](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223118.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
2. ![item:Experimental Hexplate](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223073.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
3. ![item:Fiendhunter Bolts](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/222512.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
4. ![item:Lich Bane](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223100.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
5. ![item:Nashor's Tooth](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223115.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
6. ![item:Archangel's Staff](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/323003.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Of these, Hexplate, Fiendhunter Bolts, and Malignance are the ones supplying Ultimate Ability Haste.

This build ends up giving R roughly **260 Ability Haste**.

Cover the remaining haste with augments like Eureka, Infinite Recursion, and Shrink Engine.

---

## Route 2: Mystic Punch On-Hit Build

This route comes online far more easily than the Archmage CD build.

Core augment:

- ![augment:Mystic Punch](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1058.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Recommended pairings:

- ![augment:Dual Wield](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1225.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Double Tap](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2010.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Typhoon](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1087.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Ethereal Weapon](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1029.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

All of these add extra attacks or on-hit procs, which raises how efficiently Mystic Punch triggers.

### How It Works

Mystic Punch keeps shaving cooldown off your abilities through on-hit effects.

Kayle is already a high attack speed, on-hit champion, and paired with items that re-trigger on-hit effects, a single string of autos can generate a huge number of Mystic Punch procs.

This route does not require pushing your ult's base CD down to 7 seconds.

In practice all you need is:

> **First get R's actual cooldown under 40 seconds**

Then use high attack speed plus a pile of on-hit effects to keep proccing Mystic Punch during the fight after you ult, burning off the remaining tens of seconds of CD fast.

The end result:

> ult for invulnerability
> → keep auto attacking
> → proc Mystic Punch over and over
> → R refreshes quickly
> → ult again

---

## Mystic Punch Recommended Build

1. **Experimental Hexplate**
2. **Fiendhunter Bolts**
3. **Statikk Shiv**
4. **Guinsoo's Rageblade**
5. **Dusk and Dawn**
6. **Runaan's Hurricane**

Breaking that down:

- **Hexplate, Fiendhunter Bolts**: supply Ultimate Ability Haste to get R under 40 seconds first
- **Statikk**: the chain lightning creates extra on-hit procs
- **Rageblade**: the double attack raises your proc count
- **Dusk and Dawn**: empowers and repeats on-hit effects
- **Hurricane**: the split bolts add more on-hit procs

The goal of this build isn't simply to raise Kayle's auto attack damage, it's:

> one auto attack
> → generate as many on-hit procs as possible
> → trigger Mystic Punch multiple times
> → shred R's cooldown

The higher your attack speed and the more extra attacks you have, the faster the ult refreshes.

---

## In Game

### Archmage Route

The key is being disciplined with your abilities:

> R → W → R → W

Don't throw out Q and E for no reason, or Archmage's cooldown refund gets siphoned off onto other abilities that are already on cooldown.

Once R is under 7 seconds, you can start running the W-R loop.

### Mystic Punch Route

Here the key is keeping your attacks flowing:

> R to engage
> → start auto attacking at full speed
> → Statikk, Rageblade, Dusk and Dawn, and Hurricane keep firing on-hit procs
> → Mystic Punch refreshes R quickly
> → ult again on the next cycle

Which means the Mystic Punch build is especially afraid of:

- getting crowd controlled
- getting disarmed
- not being able to reach anyone
- an enemy team full of ranged kiting champions

The moment your attack rhythm breaks, the ult stops refreshing reliably.

---

## How Do You Choose Between Them?

### Archmage CD Build

Pros:

- The infinite R mechanic is much more direct
- You don't have to keep attacking someone to refresh
- Once online, W and R just loop on their own

Cons:

- The haste requirement is extremely steep
- Fairly dependent on the Archmage + Caster combo
- Demanding item and augment requirements

### Mystic Punch Build

Pros:

- Much lower bar to come online
- R only needs to get under about 40 seconds
- Kayle is a natural fit for attack speed and on-hit items
- Dual Wield, Double Tap, Typhoon, and Ethereal Weapon all have solid synergy

Cons:

- You have to keep attacking enemies
- Vulnerable to CC and ranged kiting
- Infinite R is impossible without a safe window to auto attack

Putting it together:

> **The Archmage build is the extreme-CD mutual-refresh gimmick; the Mystic Punch build is the more practical, easier-to-assemble infinite R route.**

## Notes

- The tested target for the Archmage route is an R cooldown below about 7 seconds.
- On the Archmage route, W's 15 second base gives R about 4.5 seconds of refund.
- The Mystic Punch route only needs R under about 40 seconds first, then keeps refreshing it with on-hit effects.
- On the Mystic Punch build, don't just stack normal Ability Haste — attack speed and extra attack procs matter every bit as much.
- Hexplate and Fiendhunter Bolts work on both routes; their main value is Ultimate Ability Haste.
- Infinite R doesn't mean permanent invulnerability — you can still die when you get CC'd, can't attack, or the loop breaks.
- Exact cooldown thresholds and specific on-hit interactions can shift with patches, so trust the actual in-game CD.

guides.title: Infinite R Ashe: Archmage E-R Mutual Refresh
guides.summary: Use “Archmage,” which refunds cooldown based on an ability's original cooldown, to keep Ashe's E and R on the same base cooldown. Once you hit around 70% cooldown reduction, E and R fully refresh each other.
guides.gameplay:
## Core Mechanic

Here's what "Archmage" does:

> After you cast an ability, it refunds cooldown to another random ability equal to 30% of the cast ability's original cooldown.

The refund is based on the **original cooldown**, so it doesn't shrink as you stack Ability Haste.

Ashe's max rank R has a 60 second base cooldown, so every R cast refunds:

> 60 × 30% = 18 seconds of cooldown

Ashe's E at rank 4 also has a 60 second base charge cooldown. Casting E likewise refunds 18 seconds to R.

Once both E and R have actual cooldowns under 18 seconds, you get:

> E refunds 18 seconds to R
> → R refreshes instantly
> → R refunds 18 seconds to E
> → E refreshes instantly
> → repeat the E-R loop

## Three Requirements

### 1. You have to get Archmage

This is the irreplaceable core augment for the entire build.

Without Archmage, even a mountain of Ability Haste only shortens your ult cooldown — you can't get E and R to instantly refresh each other.

### 2. Around 70% cooldown reduction

At 70% CDR, a 60 second base cooldown becomes 18 seconds.

That works out to roughly:

> 234 Ability Haste

The video treats 230+ as the practical threshold. Factoring in cast animations and cooldown ticking naturally, the loop may already work close to 230, but the safer benchmark is hitting 70% cooldown reduction on your stat page.

### 3. E can only go to rank 4

This is the easiest part to get wrong.

Ashe's E base charge cooldown drops as you rank it up:

- Rank 4 E: 60 seconds
- Rank 5 E: 50 seconds

If you put E to rank 5, casting E only refunds:

> 50 × 30% = 15 seconds

But R's actual cooldown is around 18 seconds, so about 3 seconds are left over and the E-R loop breaks.

Your final skill levels should stay at:

> Q at 5
> W at 5
> E at 4
> R at 3

Don't spend your last skill point.

## Recommended Items

The full six item build is:

1. **Imperial Mandate**
2. **Malignance**
3. **Axiom Arc**
4. **Horizon Focus**
5. **Rabadon's Deathcap**
6. **Cryptbloom**

Excluding Deathcap, the other five items give you about 100 Ability Haste combined.

That means you still need roughly 130 more Ability Haste from augments to reach the E-R loop threshold.

This build also covers:

- Ability Haste
- Ultimate Ability Haste
- bonus damage on long-range abilities
- crowd control and team value once your ult lands
- Axiom Arc's cooldown refund on kills
- late game AP and ult damage

## Recommended Haste Augments

Besides Archmage, these five augments are recommended to top off your Ability Haste:

- **Purist - Caster**
- **Shrink Engine**
- **Ultimate Awakening**
- **Eureka**
- **Infinite Recursion**

## In Game

Once you're fully online, the loop is dead simple:

1. Make sure Q and W aren't on cooldown.
2. Cast E in any direction.
3. E refreshes R through Archmage.
4. Immediately fire R at the enemy.
5. R refreshes E through Archmage.
6. Cast E again.
7. Repeat.

The loop is:

> E → R → E → R → E → R

E doesn't need to hit an enemy — simply casting it triggers Archmage — so once you're online you can run the whole loop standing in fountain.

Ults fired from fountain travel an enormous distance, which also makes it easier to hit the longer stun durations.

## Notes

- E must absolutely never go to rank 5, or a single cast only refunds 15 seconds.
- Try not to cast Q or W during the loop so Archmage's random refund doesn't get siphoned off onto other abilities.
- Make sure both E and R are in a state where they can refresh each other before you start the loop.
- Right at the threshold you may occasionally get a brief gap; padding out a bit more haste makes it more consistent.
- Axiom Arc isn't required for the E-R loop; it's mainly there for extra refreshes after kills and some margin for error.
- Infinite R doesn't automatically mean high ult damage — Deathcap, Horizon Focus, and AP still matter a lot.
- Crowd control effectiveness drops off noticeably when the enemy has spell shields, cleanse, Zhonya's, or CC immunity abilities.
- This build leans on Archmage's special cooldown interaction, which may get adjusted in a later patch.

## Playstyle Summary

The core formula for infinite R Ashe is:

> Archmage
> ＋ rank 4 E's 60 second base cooldown
> ＋ max rank R's 60 second base cooldown
> ＋ about 70% cooldown reduction
> ＝ E and R refunding 18 seconds to each other

Once you're fully online, all you do is keep repeating:

> E refreshes R
> → R refreshes E
> → E refreshes R

and you can fire Enchanted Crystal Arrow after Enchanted Crystal Arrow, chain-locking enemy champions from inside your own fountain.

guides.title: Infinite R Tryndamere
guides.summary: If you get Mystic Punch early and the enemy has a lot of frontline and little crowd control, you can chain ults forever by attacking at high frequency to burn down your R cooldown.
guides.gameplay:
## How It Works

> Use Mystic Punch's auto-attack cooldown reduction together with Double Tap, Dual Wield, and multi-hit items to refresh your next ultimate while the current one is still running, giving you absurdly high ult uptime.

This build doesn't literally make Tryndamere's ult zero cooldown — it steadily eats away at the ult's remaining cooldown through sustained auto attacks.

Normally, one auto attack triggers one Mystic Punch proc, which is about 1.25 seconds of cooldown.

If you pair it with Double Tap or Dual Wield, a single auto attack generates an extra attack or on-hit proc, so Mystic Punch fires twice — one auto attack shaves off about 2.5 seconds of cooldown.

Add items like Statikk, Rageblade, and Dusk and Dawn that create multi-target or extra attacks, and you can push the Mystic Punch proc count much higher still.

The core logic of the whole build is:

> lower the ult's base cooldown
> → keep auto attacking after you ult
> → extra attacks proc Mystic Punch repeatedly
> → rapidly burn down the ult's remaining cooldown
> → refresh the next ult before the current one expires

So what this build actually cares about isn't how much damage a single auto does, it's how many attack procs one auto attack can generate.

## Augment Choices

### ![augment:Mystic Punch](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1058.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The irreplaceable core augment for the entire build.

Auto attacks reduce your remaining ability cooldowns, letting Tryndamere actively refresh his ult by continuing to auto attack instead of waiting for it to come back naturally.

Without Mystic Punch, even a fully completed build struggles to chain ults, so I don't recommend forcing this build without it.

### ![augment:Double Tap](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2010.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Adds an extra attack or on-hit proc, so a single auto attack generates more Mystic Punch triggers.

Combined with Statikk's multi-target effect, it visibly speeds up your ult refresh, making it one of the highest-priority augments after Mystic Punch itself.

### ![augment:Dual Wield](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1225.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Serves a similar purpose to Double Tap — its core value is likewise more attacks or extra attack procs.

For infinite R Tryndamere, extra attacks not only add damage, they keep proccing Mystic Punch, so their value far exceeds a plain damage augment.

### Other Augment Options

![augment:Infinite Recursion](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1388.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1) ![augment:Ethereal Weapon](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1029.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1) ![augment:Ultimate Revolution](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1088.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

## Recommended Build

### ![item:Experimental Hexplate](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223073.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)  ![item:Fiendhunter Bolts](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/222512.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

These two items are mainly there to provide Ultimate Ability Haste and lower the base cooldown of Tryndamere's ult.

Together they supply roughly 60 Ultimate Ability Haste.

The shorter the ult's base cooldown, the less time Mystic Punch has to shave off, and the easier it becomes to chain ults.

### ![item:Statikk Shiv](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223087.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Statikk is the single most important multi-target refresh item in this build.

Its lightning can hit multiple units, and every one of those hits has a chance to proc Mystic Punch.

Say Statikk hits 6 targets:

> 6 Mystic Punch procs × 1.25 seconds
> = about 7.5 seconds of cooldown removed

If you also have Double Tap or Dual Wield making the attack effect proc one extra time:

> 6 targets × 2 procs × 1.25 seconds
> = about 15 seconds of cooldown removed

So in environments crowded with enemies, minions, or summons, a single Statikk proc can massively cut into Tryndamere's ult cooldown.

Statikk's refresh efficiency is heavily dependent on target count:

- The more targets it hits, the bigger the cooldown reduction.
- Against a single target, your refresh speed drops noticeably.
- Waves, summons, and clumped enemy positioning all raise Statikk's value.

### ![item:Guinsoo's Rageblade](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223124.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Rageblade mainly supplies attack speed and extra-attack effects.

Attack speed raises how many autos you land per second, and the extra attacks keep proccing Mystic Punch, so it's a perfect fit for this build.

Compared to simply adding attack damage, Rageblade's more important value is raising your attack proc frequency so Tryndamere burns through the ult's remaining cooldown faster.

### ![item:Dusk and Dawn](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/222510.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Dusk and Dawn generates extra attacks or multi-hit attack procs.

Those extra attacks keep proccing Mystic Punch, and can chain into Double Tap, Dual Wield, and similar effects all over again.

Its main job isn't raising burst damage, it's making every auto attack produce more cooldown-reduction procs.

### ![item:Wit's End](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223091.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Wit's End is mainly for topping off attack speed, magic resist, and tenacity.

What infinite R Tryndamere fears most isn't enemy damage — it's getting chain crowd controlled so you can't auto attack.

If Tryndamere gets stunned, knocked up, or rooted for an extended period during his ult, he can't keep proccing Mystic Punch and the next ult may not refresh in time.

The tenacity from Wit's End shortens some of that crowd control and gives you more margin for error when chaining ults.

## In Game

### Early Game

Once you have Mystic Punch you can start building toward infinite R, but with weak early items and low attack speed you still won't be able to genuinely chain ults.

Early on, keep in mind:

- Don't dive into all five of them just because you picked up Mystic Punch.
- Prioritize Ultimate Ability Haste and attack speed items.
- Try to attack melee champions or frontliners who will stand there and trade with you.
- Don't ult early when there's nothing to auto attack.
- Save your dash or chase tools so enemies can't easily disengage.

### Mid Game

Once you've built your Ultimate Ability Haste items and Statikk, the build starts having real combat power.

In teamfights, play it like this:

1. Wait for the enemy to burn some of their crowd control first.
2. Get on top of the closest, easiest target to keep hitting.
3. Only ult once your health drops into the danger zone.
4. After ulting, keep auto attacking — don't stop dealing damage.
5. Try to position Statikk hits where enemies are clumped together.
6. Watch the remaining cooldown on your next ult.
7. If your ult is about to expire and the next one hasn't refreshed yet, back off in time.

At this stage, don't force your way past the frontline to chase the backline.

For infinite R Tryndamere, a frontliner you can keep hitting is the tool that refreshes your ult. Stopping your attacks for a long stretch to chase a squishy is more likely to break your ult loop.

### Late Game

With items and augments fully assembled, Tryndamere can maintain extremely high ult uptime in teamfights.

Recommended sequence:

1. Let your teammates or the enemy start the fight first.
2. Get close to a target you can keep attacking.
3. Don't ult early at full health.
4. Pop your first ult when you're low.
5. Keep attacking the nearest enemy.
6. Use Statikk to hit multiple champions, minions, or summons.
7. Repeatedly proc Mystic Punch with Rageblade, Dusk and Dawn, and your extra-attack augments.
8. Once the next ult refreshes, stay on the field and keep dealing damage.
9. If the refresh fails, use a dash or move speed to back off in time.

## Good Matchups

This build works well when:

- The enemy team has a lot of melee champions.
- The enemy has multiple frontliners.
- Teamfights last a long time.
- Enemies position fairly tightly together.
- There are frequently waves or summons on the field.
- The enemy has little hard crowd control.
- Tryndamere can reliably close the gap and keep auto attacking.
- Your team can provide speed ups, shields, or crowd control.

Facing multiple frontliners actually makes this build easier to pull off.

That's because frontliners generally won't disengage quickly, letting Tryndamere auto attack steadily and continuously proc Mystic Punch to refresh his ult.

## Bad Matchups

Don't force this build when:

- You didn't get Mystic Punch.
- The enemy has a lot of ranged poke champions.
- The enemy has tons of knockups, stuns, and roots.
- The enemy is highly mobile and Tryndamere struggles to keep attacking.
- The enemy has disarms, blinds, or untargetability.
- Teamfight burst is so high that fights end almost immediately.
- There are no waves or extra targets on the field, so Statikk can't do its job.
- Your team lacks engage and speed ups, so Tryndamere can barely get close.

## Common Failure Points

### Not attacking a target consistently

This build refreshes the ult through auto attacks.

If the enemy all disengages, or Tryndamere spends ages chasing the backline without reaching anything, Mystic Punch never procs.

### Getting chain crowd controlled

You can't auto attack while you're crowd controlled, which means you can't reduce your ult cooldown.

Right as your first ult is about to end especially, one long crowd control can break the entire loop outright.

### Statikk hitting too few targets

Statikk's value in multi-target versus single-target environments is night and day.

If Statikk only hits one target, you won't come close to the refresh speed shown in the video.

### Not enough attack speed

Even if every attack reduces your cooldown, if your attack interval is too long the next ult still may not refresh in time.

### Ulting too early

Ulting ahead of time at full or high health wastes a large chunk of the ult's duration.

The better approach is to eat some damage first and ult once your health drops into the danger zone.

### Force-chasing the backline

The core of infinite R Tryndamere is maintaining attack frequency, not necessarily attacking squishies first.

Stopping your auto attacks for a long stretch to chase the backline is more likely to break your ult loop.

## Notes

- Without Mystic Punch, don't force the infinite R build path.
- This build isn't literally zero cooldown — the actual result depends on target count, attack speed, and proc luck.
- The more targets Statikk hits, the faster your ult refreshes.
- Refresh efficiency drops off sharply in single-target situations.
- Don't stop auto attacking for long stretches just to chase the backline.
- When you're chain crowd controlled, you can still get ult downtime even with a finished build.
- Wit's End is mainly there for margin of error against crowd control comps, not a mandatory buy.

guides.title: Long-Range Crit Jayce
guides.summary: Crit Jayce no longer relies purely on QE poke from range — instead he uses the high attack speed of cannon form W to land several crits in quick succession. Early and mid game you play around ability burst and melee entries; once your crit items are online, you shift into sustained marksman-style damage.
guides.gameplay:
## How It Works

Traditional lethality Jayce leans on QE accelerated shots to poke, but once those abilities go on cooldown his sustained damage is fairly limited.

The crit build instead uses the huge attack speed from Jayce's cannon form W to fire off three auto attacks in rapid succession. Once your crit items are online, all three of those attacks can crit, letting you delete a squishy at close range in an instant.

Going crit doesn't mean giving up on QE entirely. Before a fight starts you can still poke with QE, and once it lands, look for the range to follow up with AW for the burst.

The full game plan is:

> QE poke from range
> → look for an entry window in hammer form
> → swap to cannon form and auto attack to shred their resistances
> → W to unload crits fast
> → once they're on top of you, swap back to hammer to keep hitting or knock them away

## Augment Choices

Crit Jayce has no single mandatory core augment. Your picks revolve around crit, attack range, and survivability.

### Crit Augments

Prioritize:

- ![augment:Critical Missile](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1356.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Upgrade Infinity Edge](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1336.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Jeweled Gauntlet](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1048.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

These raise your crit value or add burst to your auto attacks and abilities.

If you get Jeweled Gauntlet, Jayce's QE and hammer form abilities also get a chance to scale off your crit items.

### Attack Range Augments

Jayce counts as melee when he swaps to hammer form, so swap to hammer before you take Scoped Weapons.

Options:

- ![augment:Scoped Weapons](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1170.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Scopier Weapons](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1071.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Scopiest Weapons](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1115.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

## Recommended Build

### ![item:Hubris](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/226697.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Before your items are online, Jayce still needs QE poke from range.

Note that Jayce's melee form and ranged form track Hubris stacks separately. To get the growth stat higher, you can't spend the whole game poking in cannon form — you also need to look for chances to get kills in hammer form.

### ![item:The Collector](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/667666.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The Collector gives attack damage, lethality, and crit chance all at once, which fits Jayce's hybrid damage profile well.

QE, hammer form abilities, and auto attacks all benefit from the AD and lethality, and the execute helps Jayce finish off low health targets.

If the enemy has a lot of shields you can swap this for Serpent's Fang depending on their comp; if you need mobility, consider a different lethality item.

### ![item:Lord Dominik's Regards](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223036.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Lord Dominik's Regards provides crit chance and percentage armor penetration.

Crit Jayce doesn't just attack squishies — he may need to deal with the enemy frontline too. Percentage armor pen keeps your auto attacks from bouncing off high armor champions later in the game.

### ![item:Infinity Edge](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223031.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Infinity Edge is the core damage item for the crit build.

As your crit chance fills out, IE noticeably raises the burst on your AW attack chain. An enemy squishy can usually be deleted with one W and three autos.

## Good Matchups

Crit Jayce is a solid pick when:

- The enemy has a lot of squishy champions.
- Jayce has the space to get into auto attack range.
- The enemy lacks assassins who can instantly delete Jayce.

The crit build has much stronger late game sustained damage than pure lethality. Even when your QE misses, you can still put out steady damage with auto attacks.

## Bad Matchups

Don't force it in these situations:

- The enemy has a lot of ranged poke champions.
- The enemy clearly outranges Jayce.
- The enemy has multiple strong engage and hard crowd control champions.
- Enemy assassins can easily close on Jayce and delete him.
- Your team has no frontline at all.

If you can't safely auto attack all game, crit items lose most of their value, and pure lethality poke is probably the better choice.

## Common Failure Points

### Only firing cannon shots from the back

The crit build's main advantage comes from W-empowered auto attacks.

If you only ever use QE and never step into auto attack range, most of the value of your crit items goes unused.

### Sitting in cannon form permanently

Your first auto attack after swapping from hammer form to cannon form shreds the target's resistances.

Sitting in cannon form permanently gives up that important resistance shred, and you also lose out on the resistances and melee abilities hammer form provides.

### Bad W timing

Cannon form W has a limited duration.

Once you activate it, attack your target immediately. If you pop W and then spend time walking around looking for someone, you'll waste the empowered autos.

## Notes

- Going crit doesn't mean abandoning QE — the ranged cannon is still an important poke and engage tool.
- W's three empowered auto attacks should be fired off quickly from a safe distance.
- Ideally swap from hammer form to cannon form before starting your AW burst, so the first auto shreds their resistances.
- Play like a fighter or assassin in the early and mid game, then transition to marksman play once your crit items are online.
- Manamune isn't a mandatory item — in a fast-paced game, or if your skillshot accuracy is low, it can slow down your crit item spike.
- When there's no safe window to auto attack, don't force your way into the enemy team.
- Jayce is extremely reliant on managing both forms; if you're not practiced, it's easy to fumble the ability-to-attack transitions.

guides.title: Back To Basics Illaoi: Land E and Delete Them Through the Spirit
guides.summary: Stack health like crazy around Heartsteel early, pick up Back To Basics and lose your ultimate along the way, then use Overlord's Bloodmail to turn that health into AD — ending up with an Illaoi who plays like a “poke fighter,” ripping out spirits with E and bursting people down from range.
guides.gameplay:
## Core Concept

Back To Basics seals Illaoi's ultimate while buffing the damage, healing, and cast frequency of her basic abilities.

For a traditional Illaoi, having no ultimate means losing her single most important 1-vs-many tool; but once you've stacked a huge pile of health from Heartsteel and Tank Engine and then add Overlord's Bloodmail, you can convert all that health into a massive amount of AD.

The damage transfer rate on Illaoi's E spirit scales with AD, so the more health you have, the more AD Overlord's Bloodmail gives you, and the more damage gets passed back to the real body when you hit the spirit.

The build turns her from "ult in and brawl" into:

> Sit behind your teammates looking for E
> → Rip out an enemy's spirit
> → Focus the spirit
> → Huge damage transfers to the enemy's real body
> → Even if they walk away, they can still get drained out

Late game, at close to 10,000 health and 570 AD, E's spirit damage transfer rate gets close to 99% — whatever damage the spirit takes, the enemy body takes basically all of it too.

---

## Recommended Augments

### ![augment:Back To Basics](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1004.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The core augment of the entire build.

The cost is that you can't use your ultimate, but your basic ability damage and cast frequency get buffed. Once you have it, stop charging into the crowd to engage like a traditional Illaoi — play around E for mid-range poke instead.

### ![augment:Steel Your Heart](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1152.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Used to get and upgrade the Heartsteel package.

Illaoi has a pretty easy time getting close to the frontline to proc Heartsteel, and the permanent health she stacks also feeds AD into Overlord's Bloodmail later.

### ![augment:Tank Engine](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1353.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Kills and assists keep pushing your max health higher.

Together with Heartsteel it handles the base HP stacking, so Illaoi ends up getting tankiness, AD, and shield value all at the same time.

## Build Order

### 1.  ![item:Heartsteel](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223084.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The health foundation of the whole build.

Hitting enemy champions keeps stacking permanent health; that health improves your survivability now and converts into AD later through Overlord's Bloodmail.

The earlier you start stacking Heartsteel in this build, the higher your late-game ceiling.

### 2.  ![item:Black Cleaver](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223071.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Black Cleaver second solves two problems:

- It gives Ability Haste, so E, Q, and W come up more often
- It gives armor shred, which raises your real damage when you're hitting the spirit

Illaoi's abilities and tentacles stack Cleaver quickly, so the value is pretty consistent whether you're hitting the frontline or a spirit.

### 3.  ![item:Overlord's Bloodmail](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/447111.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Overlord's Bloodmail gives AD based on bonus health. All the HP you piled up from Heartsteel and Tank Engine converts straight into a huge AD number the moment it's finished.

This item turns what was a plain HP-stacking build into:

> More health
> → More AD from Overlord's Bloodmail
> → More spirit transfer damage from E
> → More damage from W and tentacles too

---

## How to Play It

## Early Game: Just Stack HP

Before you've picked up Back To Basics, keep playing standard Illaoi:

- Actively look for chances to proc Heartsteel
- Stack Tank Engine through kills and assists
- Take fights where you have tentacles up
- Use E to pull spirits and poke the enemy
- Don't mindlessly run into a ranged comp just to stack Heartsteel

## After Back To Basics: Change Your Positioning

Once you lose the ult, you can't think of yourself as a traditional Illaoi anymore.

From here you should dive in a lot less — stand in the mid-to-back line or behind your frontline and use your high Ability Haste to throw E constantly.

Recommended damage pattern:

> E to rip out the spirit
> → W the spirit and trigger tentacles
> → Q to hit the spirit and the body at once
> → Keep hitting the spirit
> → Wait for the damage to transfer to the enemy's body

If the enemy body and their spirit are standing close together, try to land Q and tentacles on both at once for double pressure.

## Once Overlord's Bloodmail Is Online: Play It Like a Poke Champ

After Bloodmail is finished, E becomes a real threat.

At this point you don't have to force damage onto the enemy body — you just need to land E:

- Pull a frontliner and you can chunk them down fast
- Pull a squishy and you might leave the body nearly dead
- Pull a low-health champion and just hitting the spirit finishes the kill from range
- When they push forward to fight back, use your Sterak's shield and W to counterattack up close

Late in the video, Illaoi is basically played as a poke champion: whoever gets hit by E eats a burst of near-true damage from the spirit.

---

## Good Matchups

This build works well when:

- You get Steel Your Heart early and can start stacking Heartsteel right away
- You have the key core augment: Back To Basics
- You also have health-scaling augments like Tank Engine
- The enemy has clunky frontliners who are easy to hit with E

The clunkier the enemy frontline, the easier it is for Illaoi to keep ripping spirits out of them for steady poke.

## Bad Matchups

You'll have a hard time in these spots:

- E is very hard to land
- The enemy team has tons of dashes and movement speed
- Nobody else on your team can engage or soak damage
- Your Heartsteel stacks are too low early

Without the ult, Illaoi's ability to fight back when several people are on top of her drops off hard, so she's especially afraid of hard engage and chain CC.

---

## Things to Watch Out For

- Back To Basics flat-out seals your ultimate; once you take it you have to change traditional Illaoi's positioning and playstyle.
- This damage depends on the health synergy between Heartsteel, Tank Engine, and Overlord's Bloodmail — Back To Basics on its own won't necessarily get you there.
- E is your main damage source; if you keep whiffing it, you're almost no threat at all.
- Don't stand somewhere dangerous just to keep hitting the spirit — back off first when the enemy is setting up a hard engage.

guides.title: Infinite W Vladimir: Permanent Pool, Permanently Untouchable
guides.summary: Use Infernal Conduit's multi-target burn to continuously refund cooldown so Vladimir gets W back before the current pool even ends.
guides.gameplay:
## How It Works

Vladimir's W pool is an area damage-over-time ability — while he's in it he can't be targeted, and it damages enemies in range while healing him.

The core augment of this build is ![augment:Infernal Conduit](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1045.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1).

Infernal Conduit makes your ability damage apply a stacking burn, and while that burn is ticking it refunds cooldown on your basic abilities.

When Vladimir's W hits multiple enemies at once:

> W deals area damage to several people
> → Stacks Infernal Conduit on every target
> → The burns on all of them tick at the same time
> → W's cooldown keeps getting refunded
> → W comes back up before the current pool even ends

Based on testing:

- W's Ability Haste needs to reach roughly **160**
- The pool needs to hit **two or more enemies** at once

That's basically enough to keep W refreshing off Infernal Conduit forever.

The more enemies there are, the more densely the burn ticks and the more reliably W refreshes. So the best environment for this build isn't a 1v1 — it's a teamfight where the enemy is grouped up.

---

## Core Augment

### ![augment:Infernal Conduit](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1045.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The single most important augment on the standard infinite-W route.

It doesn't just add burn damage — more importantly, the burns on multiple enemies all refund basic ability cooldown at the same time.

Without Infernal Conduit, stacking to about 160 Ability Haste from items alone usually still isn't enough to chain pools reliably.

### Recommended Support Augments

- ![augment:Eureka](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1030.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Back To Basics](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1004.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:High Roller](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2095.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Bread And Jam](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1150.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Infinite Recursion](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1388.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![augment:Pursuit of Haste](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2100.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The selection logic is simple: prioritize basic Ability Haste, or anything that refunds ability cooldown.

Among those, Back To Basics gives up your ultimate but concentrates more power into your basic abilities. For a Vladimir built entirely around W, the ultimate matters less than it does in a normal build, so that cost is acceptable.

---

## Standard Build

This item set gives you roughly **105 Ability Haste** in total.

The rest of the Ability Haste has to come from augments, stat shards, and late-game stat shards.

### ![item:Hextech Rocketbelt](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223152.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives AP, health, and Ability Haste.

The active dash helps Vladimir get into the enemy group quickly so W covers more targets at once, which improves Infernal Conduit's cooldown refund rate.

### ![item:Riftmaker](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/224633.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Great for staying inside the enemy formation and fighting for a long time.

Vladimir can drag fights out by repeatedly pooling, so he has an easy time getting full value out of Riftmaker's extended-combat scaling.

### ![item:Cosmic Drive](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/224629.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives Ability Haste and movement speed.

The movement speed helps Vladimir reposition after a pool ends so he can stay stuck to the enemy and not get kited away before the next W comes back.

### ![item:Horizon Focus](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/224628.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Adds more AP and Ability Haste, boosting your area abilities and damage over time.

### ![item:Rabadon's Deathcap](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223089.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Once you're past the Ability Haste threshold, Deathcap massively raises your AP, boosting W, E, and ultimate damage while also strengthening Vladimir's healing.

### ![item:Cryptbloom](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223137.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

A late-game AP and Ability Haste item that further improves the consistency and damage ceiling of infinite W.

These six items don't have a fixed purchase order. Early on, prioritize Ability Haste and the ability to get in; once you're past the infinite-W threshold, add high-AP items like Deathcap.

---

## God Route 1: Purist - Caster

If you get **Purist - Caster**, you can take a different Ability Haste route.

The effect:

- Gives a flat ~10% cooldown reduction
- Converts your attack speed into Ability Haste

Testing shows that once you hit about **345** Ability Haste, you can chain W continuously without fully relying on Infernal Conduit's multi-target burn.

That number is extremely high, though, so you'll usually still need one or two gold cooldown stats from late-game stat shards.

### Build Adjustments

Once you have Purist - Caster, you can take these out of the standard build:

- ![item:Hextech Rocketbelt](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223152.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![item:Riftmaker](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/224633.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

And replace them with:

- ![item:Nashor's Tooth](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223115.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![item:Lich Bane](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223100.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The attack speed on Nashor's Tooth gets converted into Ability Haste by Purist - Caster, helping Vladimir push toward the higher cooldown numbers.

This route asks more from your stats, but once you're over the threshold you're no longer forced to hit multiple targets with every pool.

---

## God Route 2: Archmage

**Archmage** is one of the best cooldown augments for Vladimir.

Casting one ability refunds about 30% of the remaining cooldown on your other abilities.

Vladimir can use W and E to refresh each other:

> Cast W
> → Refunds E's cooldown
> → Cast E
> → Refunds W's cooldown
> → Pool again

Late game with enough Ability Haste, alternating W and E makes infinite W pretty comfortable.

This route comes online more easily than stacking to absurd Ability Haste. Just be careful not to dump all your basic abilities at once — keep W and E alternating.

---

## Easter Egg Route: ADAPt

If you see the prismatic augment **ADAPt**, take it — same recommendation.

This route ditches the traditional mage build and prioritizes health and AD instead, then uses the augment's stat conversion to reach absurd AP numbers.

Recommended items:

1. Heartsteel
2. Overlord's Bloodmail
3. Spear of Shojin
4. Cosmic Drive
5. Riftmaker
6. Rabadon's Deathcap

The core synergy:

> Heartsteel stacks max health
> → Overlord's Bloodmail converts health into AD
> → ADAPt amplifies that further into AP
> → Deathcap raises the final AP number again

In an ideal late game, your AP can break 10,000.

This route gets both the huge health pool from Heartsteel and Overlord's Bloodmail and absurd AP. Once you're in the pool you're not only nearly impossible to deal with, you can also outright kill people with the massive damage on W and E.

10,000 AP is the ideal ceiling with augments, items, and scaling all fully online — a normal game won't reliably get there.

---

## How to Play It

### Before It Comes Online

Until infinite W is online, Vladimir still has to be careful about when he goes in.

Early on your main jobs are:

- Get Ability Haste items as fast as possible
- Keep your health topped up with Q
- Use E for area poke
- Don't dive into the crowd when W is on a long cooldown
- Save W to dodge key CC and burst

W costs your own health, and spamming pools before the build is online can drop your own state fast.

### Once It's Online

Once you hit the Ability Haste requirement, actively look for spots where several enemies are grouped up.

Recommended sequence:

1. Use Rocketbelt or movement speed to close in on the enemy group.
2. Charge E, then get into the middle of them.
3. Pop W so the pool hits at least two enemies.
4. Use Infernal Conduit's multi-target burn to refresh the cooldown.
5. Follow up with Q or E when the pool ends.
6. Pool again the instant W refreshes.
7. Stay near multiple enemies — don't drift out of Infernal Conduit's proc range.

Once it's online, you don't need to chase down a single low-health champion. The tighter the enemy is packed, the more reliably W refreshes and the harder Vladimir is to target and kill.

---

## Good Matchups

This build works well when:

- The enemy has a lot of melee and frontline champions
- The enemy tends to group up
- Teamfights go long
- Vladimir can get into the enemy group easily
- The enemy lacks long-range persistent CC
- Your team can provide speed-ups, shields, or engage help
- The game lasts long enough to build up Ability Haste items

Against a lot of short-range champions, Vladimir can reliably cover two or more people with W and Infernal Conduit keeps refunding cooldown.

---

## Bad Matchups

These situations are rough:

- The enemy is all ranged poke champions
- The enemy positions very spread out
- It's hard to hit two people with one W
- The enemy has a lot of persistent CC and zoning
- The game ends too fast to reach your Ability Haste breakpoint
- You're too far behind on gold to finish the key items
- You're chasing a single target, so Infernal Conduit isn't proccing on enough people

The standard Infernal Conduit route is heavily dependent on a multi-target environment. In a 1v1 you don't get enough burn stacks and W may not refresh before the pool ends.

---

## Things to Watch Out For

- The standard route needs Infernal Conduit, around 160 Ability Haste, and at least two targets in the pool.
- Infinite W doesn't mean you're permanently untargetable — botch the ability chain and you'll still have short windows of vulnerability.
- W costs health, so you need Q, items, and ability damage to keep healing back up.
- Don't force your way in when the enemy is fully spread out; a single target rarely refreshes W reliably.
- The Purist - Caster route needs about 345 Ability Haste, a higher bar than the normal route.
- On the Archmage route, alternate W and E — don't dump both abilities at once.
- ADAPt's 10,000 AP is an ideal late-game result, not a number you can count on every game.
- Augment and item numbers can change between patches, so go by the current in-game values.

guides.title: Archmage Gangplank: Infinite Ultimate Bombardment
guides.summary: Use Archmage to make Gangplank's E and R refund each other's cooldown; once your Ability Haste is past the threshold, you can chain barrels to refresh your ultimate and then use the ultimate to get your barrels back.
guides.gameplay:
## Core Concept

This build has to be built around ![augment:Archmage](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2087.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1).

Archmage doesn't refund "30% of the target ability's current cooldown" — it refunds cooldown on your other ability based on the **base cooldown** of the ability you just cast.

That gives abilities with long base cooldowns absolutely absurd refresh potential.

For example:

- One Gangplank barrel charge has a base recharge time of about 13 seconds
- Every E cast refunds about `13 × 30% = 3.9 seconds` of cooldown on your other ability
- Drop 5 barrels in a row and that's about 20 seconds of cooldown refunded to your ultimate

And Gangplank's max-rank ultimate has a base cooldown of about 120 seconds:

- Every ultimate cast refunds about `120 × 30% = 36 seconds` to your other abilities
- 36 seconds is roughly 3 full E charges back
- Combine that with E's natural recharge and your Ability Haste and you're back to 5 barrels

Which gives you the loop:

> Drop 5 barrels in a row
> → Refresh your ultimate
> → Cast the ultimate, refunding E cooldown
> → Get 5 barrels back
> → Refresh the ultimate again

## Requirements

The key to infinite-ult Gangplank is compressing your ultimate's real cooldown down to something 5 barrels can refresh.

The targets given in the video:

- Without a special cooldown-reduction augment, you need around 430+ Ability Haste
- With ![augment:Purist - Caster](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2018.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1), you only need about 260 Ability Haste
- On top of converting attack speed into Ability Haste, Purist - Caster also gives about 10% extra cooldown reduction

In an actual game you don't have to get all of that haste from items — augments and late-game stat shards can cover the gap.

## Recommended Build

The recommended six items are: Malignance, Blackfire Torch, Archangel's Staff, Lich Bane, Nashor's Tooth, Horizon Focus

That set on its own gives Gangplank about **200 Ability Haste**.

The remaining ~60 Ability Haste can come from augments or stat shards.

### Why Nashor's Tooth?

Nashor's gives attack speed.

With Purist - Caster, attack speed converts into Ability Haste, so Nashor's doesn't just improve Gangplank's autos and barrel-popping feel — it also keeps pushing you toward the Ability Haste you need to refresh the ultimate.

### Why AP Items?

This Gangplank's main damage no longer comes from traditional crit barrels — it comes from blanketing the map with high-frequency ultimates.

AP boosts your ultimate damage while Ability Haste keeps the loop running, so the build ends up looking a lot more like a high-haste AP mage than a standard crit Gangplank.

## Recommended Augments

### Must-Have

#### ![augment:Archmage](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2087.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The one thing the whole build depends on.

Without Archmage, E and R can't refund each other's cooldown off base cooldowns, so the infinite-ult loop from the video simply doesn't exist.

The video makes a point of this:

> Only try this build if you get Archmage on the first augment round.

### Best Pairing

#### ![augment:Purist - Caster](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2018.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

It massively lowers the Ability Haste requirement for infinite ult.

It converts attack speed into Ability Haste and gives extra cooldown reduction, making it the most consistent second core for this build.

### Other Recommended Augments

Prioritize anything that gives Ability Haste or extra cooldown reduction:

- Deft
- Zealot
- Recursion
- Shrink Engine
- Infinite Recursion
- Eureka
- Infernal Conduit

If you don't roll enough haste augments, you can also make up the Ability Haste with late-game stat shards.

## The Loop in Practice

Once it's online, the execution isn't complicated:

1. Confirm you have 5 E charges.
2. Drop 5 barrels in a row — you don't need complex barrel chains on every one.
3. Archmage accumulates about 20 seconds of ultimate cooldown refund.
4. Cast the ultimate the moment it comes up.
5. Because the ultimate's base cooldown is so long, it refunds about 36 seconds of E charge time.
6. Wait a short bit of natural recharge and you're back to 5 barrels.
7. Drop barrels again to refresh the ultimate.

The full loop in short:

> Five barrels refresh R
> → R refreshes five barrels
> → Five barrels refresh R again

As long as your Ability Haste is over the threshold, the loop keeps going.

## Teamfighting

This Gangplank doesn't have to wait for the perfect triple- or double-barrel chain like a traditional crit build.

Here, the barrels' most important job isn't damage — it's being the tool that refreshes your ultimate.

In fights you can:

- Dump all 5 barrels quickly from a safe position
- Aim the ultimate at the enemy backline, their respawn point, or tight chokepoints
- Use the ultimate to constantly restrict their movement
- Start the next loop as soon as your barrels are back
- Not delay your casts chasing barrel damage

Once online, Gangplank can drop ultimate after ultimate on the same area, keeping enemies slowed and taking damage for a long stretch.

## Things to Watch Out For

- You have to get Archmage early — don't force this build without the core augment.
- Barrels are mainly there to refresh R in this build, so don't obsess over complex barrel chains.
- If your Ability Haste is too low, the ultimate will still be on cooldown after five barrels and the loop falls apart.
- After casting the ultimate you still need natural recharge to fill the remaining barrels — it doesn't instantly restore all 5 charges.
- Malignance, Blackfire Torch, Archangel's Staff and the like are AP-oriented, so before the build is online your barrel damage will be lower than a traditional crit Gangplank's.
- Infinite ult depends heavily on Ability Haste, your augment combination, and late-game stat shards.
- The video was on the PBE or the current Mayhem patch — the thresholds may shift if the numbers get adjusted.

guides.title: Protein Shake + Mercy's Strike: One Auto Attack Deletes People
guides.summary: Use Protein Shake to convert armor and magic resist into heal and shield power, then let Mercy's Strike convert that heal and shield power into max-health magic damage — works on any support with a shield or a heal.
guides.gameplay:
## Core Concept

This build needs two key augments:

- Protein Shake
- Mercy's Strike

On its own, Mercy's Strike only deals a small amount of max-health damage.

But Protein Shake grants a large amount of heal and shield power based on your bonus armor and bonus magic resist. Mercy's Strike has very high heal and shield power scaling, so as long as you keep stacking resistances, you get all of the following at once:

- Extreme tankiness
- Extreme heal and shield power
- Big percent-health damage
- A pile of attack speed from Sword of Blossoming Dawn

The full stat conversion chain looks like this:

> Armor and magic resist
> → Protein Shake converts them into heal and shield power
> → Mercy's Strike converts that into max-health magic damage
> → Sword of Blossoming Dawn converts it into attack speed

So even though you buy nothing but tank items, you end up with absolutely absurd auto attack burst.

---

## What Mercy's Strike Does

After you use the designated support ability, your next auto attack gains:

- 300 bonus attack range
- 75% bonus attack speed
- Bonus max-health magic damage

The damage formula:

> 2.5%
> + 20% of heal and shield power
> = target's max health as magic damage

That 20% doesn't mean "20% more damage" — every 1% of heal and shield power you have keeps raising Mercy's Strike's max-health damage.

So the higher your heal and shield power, the bigger the percent damage on a single empowered auto.

---

## What Protein Shake Does

Protein Shake gives base heal and shield power, then adds more based on bonus resistances:

> 25% base heal and shield power
> + 35% per 100 bonus armor
> + 35% per 100 bonus magic resist

A normal enchanter support usually builds around AP, mana, and healing items.

This build does the exact opposite: you buy tons of armor and magic resist so Protein Shake can convert those resistances into heal and shield power.

In the end, your resistances don't just make you harder to kill — they indirectly increase Mercy's Strike's damage too.

## Recommended Full Build

The point of this build isn't the damage on the items themselves — it's stacking as much armor and magic resist as possible.

### ![item:Jak'Sho, The Protean](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/226665.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Raises both resistances once a fight has gone on for a bit.

It gives armor and magic resist at the same time, making it one of the most important items for Protein Shake. Once the passive is fully stacked, both your heal and shield power and your Mercy's Strike damage go up further.

### ![item:Force of Nature](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/224401.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives a lot of magic resist, and stacks even more once its passive fills up.

If the enemy keeps throwing magic damage at you, Force of Nature stacks fast and gives Protein Shake more heal and shield power to work with.

### ![item:Unending Despair](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/222502.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives tankiness and sustained fighting power.

This build needs fights to last long enough for Jak'Sho, Force of Nature and the rest to stack up, and Unending Despair improves your ability to stand in the fight and heal so you don't die before your stats come online.

### ![item:Randuin's Omen](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223143.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives a lot of armor, improving your survivability against crit and auto attack champions.

That armor then gets converted into heal and shield power by Protein Shake, so it's both defense and damage.

### ![item:Frozen Heart](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/323110.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives high armor and Ability Haste.

The Ability Haste lets an enchanter use the designated ability more often and keep proccing Mercy's Strike, while the high armor keeps raising your heal and shield power.

### ![item:Sword of Blossoming Dawn](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/664011.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Sword of Blossoming Dawn gives attack speed based on heal and shield power:

> Every 1% of heal and shield power
> gives 1.2% attack speed

At around 255% heal and shield power:

> 255 × 1.2
> = 306% attack speed

So this build doesn't just hit hard on a single auto — it also gets a mountain of attack speed.

An enchanter in a full set of tank items ends up with enormous attack speed and percent-health damage.

## Late-Game Stat Shards

Prioritize resistance stats on your late-game stat shards:

- Armor
- Magic resist
- Shards that give both armor and magic resist

Every bit of resistance you add gets converted into more heal and shield power by Protein Shake.

Higher heal and shield power then improves:

- Mercy's Strike's max-health damage
- The attack speed from Sword of Blossoming Dawn
- Your champion's own heals and shields

So resistance shards effectively increase your tankiness, your damage, and your utility all at once.

---

## Adjusting When the Enemy Stacks Magic Resist

Mercy's Strike deals magic damage.

If the enemy starts buying a lot of magic resist late, your actual damage drops noticeably even if your tooltip says 100% max health.

In that case, swap Sword of Blossoming Dawn for:

- ![item:Void Staff](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223135.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Sword of Blossoming Dawn is there for attack speed, but Mercy's Strike already gives bonus attack range and attack speed on its own.

Against a high-MR comp, the real damage from percent magic penetration is probably worth more than keeping Sword of Blossoming Dawn.

The adjusted logic:

> Low enemy magic resist: keep Sword of Blossoming Dawn for attack speed
> High enemy magic resist: swap to Void Staff for real damage

---

## Which Champions Work

This build isn't specific to one champion — it works on any enchanter support who can reliably proc Mercy's Strike.

Take an enchanter like Milio: champions like that usually have the following traits:

- A low-cooldown heal or shield ability
- The ability to proc Mercy's Strike frequently
- The ability to use the bonus attack range to auto safely
- Their own heals and shields also benefit from Protein Shake
- They still provide utility for the team even in full tank items

The champion's own auto attack damage doesn't matter at all.

The real damage comes from the target's max-health magic damage attached to Mercy's Strike, so even a support with zero traditional damage items can take a huge chunk out of someone with one auto.

## Things to Watch Out For

- Mercy's Strike requires using the designated ability first to empower your next auto.
- Don't waste the empowered auto on minions — avoid burning it on non-champion targets.
- Sword of Blossoming Dawn is mainly there to convert heal and shield power into attack speed; it isn't required for the damage to work.
- When the enemy has high magic resist, consider Void Staff first.
- Prioritize resistance shards on late-game stat shards — don't just chase AD or AP.

## Summary

The most unusual thing about this build is that the same resistance stats get used three separate times:

> Resistances give tankiness
> → Protein Shake converts them into heal and shield power
> → Mercy's Strike converts that into max-health damage
> → Sword of Blossoming Dawn converts it into attack speed

The end result:

> An enchanter with four or five hundred armor and two or three hundred magic resist
> who's not only nearly unkillable, but can also take more than half of someone's health bar with a single auto attack.

guides.title: Archmage Teemo: Infinite R, Shrooms Across the Whole Map
guides.summary: Use Archmage to make Teemo's W and R refund each other's cooldown, then use Purist - Caster to convert attack speed into Ability Haste. Once you're past the cooldown threshold you can loop W and R endlessly, blanketing the map in shrooms fast.
guides.gameplay:
## How It Works

This build needs two core augments at the same time:

- **Archmage**
- **Purist - Caster**

Archmage sets up the loop where W and R refresh each other, and Purist - Caster lowers the Ability Haste requirement to get there.

### How Does Archmage Refresh Abilities?

Archmage's effect:

> When you cast an ability, refund cooldown on your other abilities equal to 30% of that ability's base cooldown.

It calculates off the ability's **base cooldown**, so the refund doesn't shrink as your Ability Haste goes up.

Teemo's W has a base cooldown of about 14 seconds, so every W cast refunds this much to the ultimate:

> 14 × 30% = 4.2 seconds

Each shroom charge on Teemo's ultimate has a base recharge time of about 35 seconds, so every R cast refunds this much to W:

> 35 × 30% = 10.5 seconds

Which gives you a loop where they refresh each other:

> Cast W
> → Refunds about 4.2 seconds to R
> → Throw a shroom
> → R refunds about 10.5 seconds to W
> → W is back up
> → Keep casting W and R

The full loop:

> W → R → W → R → W → R

As long as your ultimate's real recharge time is short enough, the 4.2 seconds W gives you plus the natural cooldown ticking during your casts is enough to get the next shroom back almost immediately.

Once it's online, Teemo can throw shroom after shroom in a very short window, blanketing the waves, the brush, and the area around the enemy base.

## Cooldown Threshold

Per the video's testing, once Teemo's ultimate cooldown reduction hits about **85%**, the infinite-R loop becomes fairly consistent.

Getting there with ordinary Ability Haste alone would require absurd stats — normal items can't do it.

That's why you need **Purist - Caster**.

### What Purist - Caster Does

Purist - Caster:

- Converts attack speed into Ability Haste
- Gives about 10% extra cooldown reduction

With that extra cooldown reduction, you only need about **75% cooldown reduction** from everything else.

75% cooldown reduction corresponds to roughly:

> 300 Ability Haste

So the final target is:

> Purist - Caster provides 10% cooldown reduction
> + Items and other augments provide about 300 Ability Haste
> = The cooldown threshold needed for infinite R

## The Fixed Six-Item Build

The recommended full build: **Malignance**, **Blackfire Torch**, **Archangel's Staff**, **Lich Bane**, **Nashor's Tooth**, **Horizon Focus**

The direct Ability Haste from these items adds up to about:

> 130 Ability Haste

Lich Bane and Nashor's Tooth also give attack speed.

With Purist - Caster's conversion, that attack speed turns into roughly:

> 70 Ability Haste

So the fixed six-item build ends up providing about:

> 130 base Ability Haste
> + 70 from converted attack speed
> = 200 Ability Haste

That leaves you about 100 short of the 300 target, which you make up with later augments or stat shards.

## Why Lich Bane and Nashor's Tooth?

A normal AP Teemo takes Nashor's mainly for attack speed and auto attack damage.

In this build, attack speed has an extra layer of value:

> Attack speed
> → Converted into Ability Haste by Purist - Caster
> → Shortens the real cooldowns on W and R
> → Makes the infinite shroom loop more consistent

So Lich Bane and Nashor's aren't just damage items here — they're cooldown items for the infinite-R system.

## Other Augment Choices

Once you have Archmage and Purist - Caster, prioritize cooldown-related effects with your remaining augments.

Recommended directions include:

- **Recursion**
- **Shrink Engine**
- **Infinite Recursion**
- **Ult Bot**
- **Eureka**
- **Infernal Conduit**

These either add Ability Haste directly or refund ability cooldown some other way, helping Teemo reach 300 Ability Haste faster.

### Silver Augments

For silver augments you can take:

- **Deft**
- **Zealot**

Both mainly give attack speed.

In a normal build they're just attack speed augments; with Purist - Caster, all that attack speed gets converted into Ability Haste, so they help get infinite R online too.

## How to Play It

Before it's online, play Teemo like a normal AP Teemo — poke and place shrooms, and don't spam W and R randomly while your Ability Haste is still low.

Once you're past the cooldown threshold, the execution is very simple:

1. Make sure you have at least one shroom charge.
2. Cast W, refunding about 4.2 seconds to R.
3. Immediately cast R and plant a shroom where you want it.
4. R's base cooldown refunds about 10.5 seconds to W.
5. Cast the now-refreshed W again.
6. Throw the next shroom.
7. Keep alternating W and R.

The loop:

> W → R → W → R → W → R

You don't need to wait until you have all three shroom charges saved up.

Once it's online you should be spending shroom charges constantly and using W to get the next charge back quickly. As long as you keep alternating, you can plant a huge number of shrooms in a very short time.

## Where Should You Place the Shrooms?

With infinite R, you don't have to limit yourself to brush.

Prioritize covering:

- Where both waves meet
- The main mid-map pathways
- Brush entrances
- The path the enemy has to walk after respawning
- Around turrets
- The exit from the enemy base
- Wherever a fight is about to break out

## Summary

The core logic of infinite-R Teemo is making W and R refresh each other:

> Archmage makes W refund R's cooldown
> + The ultimate refunds W's cooldown
> + Purist - Caster lowers the cooldown threshold
> + The fixed six-item build gives about 200 Ability Haste
> + Other augments or stat shards cover the rest

Once you're at about 85% ultimate cooldown reduction, all you have to do is repeat:

> W → R → W → R

and you'll keep regenerating shroom charges, blanketing the entire map in no time.

guides.title: Empowered By The Faithful + Protein Shake = Execute From Half HP
guides.summary: Heal and shield your teammates to Bless them so they stack Empowered By The Faithful fast. Then use Protein Shake to turn a mountain of armor and magic resist into Heal and Shield Power, and you end up firing off a high-damage magic shockwave that covers about two screens.
guides.gameplay:
## Core of the Build

The core augments are:

- **Protein Shake**
- **Empowered By The Faithful**

The whole stat-conversion chain looks like this:

> Stack armor and magic resist
> → Protein Shake converts those resistances into Heal and Shield Power
> → Heal and Shield Power raises Empowered By The Faithful's damage
> → once a teammate hits 50 stacks, a massive-radius magic shockwave goes off

---

## How do you proc Empowered By The Faithful?

The biggest problem people run into with this combo is not knowing how to stack Empowered By The Faithful quickly.

Healing or shielding a teammate gives them roughly **8 seconds of Blessing**.

While Blessed, any damage that teammate deals builds stacks for Empowered By The Faithful. At **50 stacks** it releases a magic shockwave with an enormous radius.

The basic proc sequence:

> Heal or shield a teammate
> → they get 8 seconds of Blessing
> → they keep hitting enemies
> → Empowered By The Faithful reaches 50 stacks
> → a massive-radius magic shockwave goes off

The shockwave reaches close to two screens wide, so enemies can suddenly eat a huge chunk of damage even from very far away.

### Best teammates to buff

Try to funnel your heals and shields into:

- ADCs with very high attack speed
- champions with multi-hit damage
- champions that can keep hitting several targets
- core carries who get to deal damage consistently in teamfights

If you put Blessing on a teammate with long cooldowns and a low damage output rate, your stacking slows down noticeably.

---

## Why is Protein Shake the core?

Protein Shake raises your Heal and Shield Power based on how much armor and magic resist you have.

That means every resistance item you buy gives you:

- more survivability
- stronger heals
- thicker shields
- more Empowered By The Faithful damage

Armor and MR stop being purely defensive stats and become this build's main damage source.

The full synergy:

> The more armor and magic resist you have
> → the more Heal and Shield Power Protein Shake gives
> → the stronger your heals and shields
> → the higher Empowered By The Faithful's magic damage

## What if you don't get Protein Shake?

Go with the alternative build below and your execute threshold will still be over 20%.

## Build summary

> Resistances make you tanky
> → Protein Shake turns those resistances into Heal and Shield Power
> → heal or shield your high-output teammates to Bless them
> → they hit 50 stacks within the 8 seconds
> → Empowered By The Faithful fires a massive-radius magic shockwave

Once it's online you have huge resistances, big heals and AoE shields, and you can set off a high-damage shockwave covering nearly two screens from the back of your team.

guides.title: 3.0: The Thousand Blades Build Is Back
guides.summary: Vulnerability plus Critical Missile + 100% crit + Fated Ashes gets you endless missiles
