guides.title: Multishot AP Lucian
guides.summary: Once the Multishot quest is done, your W fills the whole screen. More of a for-fun build.
guides.gameplay:
> If you pick up the quest augment Multishot at the start of the game, build around Lucian's W to complete the quest. Every quest tier you finish adds another split missile to W; in a normal game you'll finish tier 4, so a single W fires five missiles. That's why you drop the traditional crit route and go pure AP ranged poke.

## Core of the build

Multishot has six quest tiers, and you have to finish one before the next unlocks.

You progress the quest by hitting enemies with the bound ability. On Lucian, that's W:

- after tier 1, W splits into 2 missiles
- every tier after that adds 1 more missile to W
- after tier 4, a single W fires 5 missiles

The full progression:

> 1 W missile
> → 2 W missiles
> → 3 W missiles
> → 4 W missiles
> → 5 W missiles

The extra missiles fan out in different directions, which hugely widens the ability's coverage. When enemies group up or stand in a tight space, one W covers most of the battlefield and turns into screen-wide magic damage.

---

## How does the quest level up?


| Quest tier | Enemies you need to hit | W missiles after |
| ---------- | ----------------------: | ---------------: |
| Tier 1     |                       4 |                2 |
| Tier 2     |                      14 |                3 |
| Tier 3     |                      34 |                4 |
| Tier 4     |                     104 |                5 |
| Tier 5     |         several hundred |                6 |
| Tier 6     |      many hundreds more |                7 |

Tiers 5 and 6 ask for far too much and are basically impossible in a normal game, so there's no need to force your way to max level.

Your real goal is finishing tier 4:

> One W splitting into 5 missiles is what "fully online" actually looks like in a normal game.

The quest feels slow early, but once tier 1 is done your W throws several missiles at once, each cast hits more enemies, and your stacking speed keeps climbing.

### Tips for farming the quest

- Aim W at the densest clump of enemies
- Quest progress is fastest during full teamfights
- Choke points and areas near turrets make it easier to hit several people at once
- Don't spend W poking a single isolated target
- Cast it whenever it's up; the earlier you clear tier 1, the faster everything after it goes

## When can you play it?

- Only go for this when you get Multishot **in the first augment round**.

The reason is that the quest needs a huge number of hits. If you only get it on the second round or later, there may not be enough game left to finish tier 4.

- It's an option when the enemy team is all squishy poke champs.

The reason is that Lucian's range is fairly short and he has a hard time touching long-range mages, so if the enemy has a lot of tanks and bruisers this build isn't recommended

---

## Bad games for it

Don't force the AP swap in these situations:

- you didn't get Multishot in the first round
- the enemy has too many bruisers or tanks
- your team has no other AD damage

AP Lucian's payoff isn't consistent, and traditional AD crit or lethality builds are usually more reliable.

## Build summary

The point of Multishot Lucian isn't auto attacks, it's turning W into a wide-area barrage:

> Get Multishot in the first round
> → complete the quest with W
> → each tier adds another split missile
> → tier 4 gives you a five-missile W
> → switch to pure AP and magic pen items
> → keep poking the whole screen from the backline

Once tier 4 is done, a single W blankets a huge area. With Luden's Echo, Horizon Focus, Deathcap and magic pen items, Lucian goes from a short-range marksman to an AP mage who bombs people from range with W.

guides.title: Infinite Ultimate Karthus
guides.summary: There are three main routes: Archmage cooldown ping-pong, Purist - Caster max Ability Haste, and Tooth Fairy paired with Axiom Arc.
guides.gameplay:
> Karthus infinite ult currently has three main routes:
>
> Archmage: refresh R with W, you need to hit 234+ Ability Haste
>
> Caster: 300+ Ability Haste, paired with Eureka or Infinite Recursion. Late game it's basically an ult every 10 seconds; this is the easiest one to pull off, and two or three of your items can be swapped for the attack speed pair
>
> Tooth Fairy: once Tooth Fairy has enough stacks, any assist off your ult resets it forever; for items, swap a big lethality item for Axiom Arc

## Route 1: Archmage W/R cooldown ping-pong

This is the cleanest mechanic of the three and the most consistent loop once it's online.

Archmage refunds cooldown to another ability whenever you cast a spell, equal to 30% of that ability's base cooldown.

Karthus's key cooldowns:

- W base cooldown: 15 seconds
- rank 3 R cooldown: 120 seconds

At 234 Ability Haste:

- W's real cooldown is about 4.49 seconds, under 15 × 30% = 4.5 seconds
- R's real cooldown is about 35.93 seconds, under 120 × 30% = 36 seconds

Which gives you:

> R → refreshes W → W → refreshes R → R

### Execution notes

Try not to throw out Q and E randomly during the loop.

Archmage refunds "another ability that's on cooldown," so if Q, E, W and R are all down at once the refund can get spread around and your W won't refresh R.

The most consistent way to run it:

1. Keep Q and E off cooldown.
2. Cast R.
3. R refunds W's cooldown.
4. Cast W immediately.
5. W refunds R's cooldown.
6. Repeat the W/R loop.

### Requirements

- You must have Archmage
- 234 or more Ability Haste on your stat sheet
- Don't let Q and E go on cooldown at the same time while looping

### Build direction

Prioritize items with high Ability Haste and AP:

- Malignance
- Blackfire Torch
- Archangel's Staff
- Horizon Focus
- Cosmic Drive
- Rabadon's Deathcap

The exact items aren't set in stone; the point is getting your Ability Haste to 234.

If your items don't get you there, top it off with these augments:

- Eureka
- Infinite Recursion
- Recursion
- Shrink Engine
- Ability Haste Forging

---

## Route 2: Purist - Caster max Ability Haste

Purist - Caster gives 10% CDR and converts all of your attack speed into Ability Haste:

> Every 1% attack speed
> → becomes 0.65 Ability Haste

Karthus has a special attack speed value while he's in his ghost state, and Caster converts that attack speed into Ability Haste too, which drops his ult cooldown by an absurd amount.

This route doesn't need the W/R juggling that Archmage does; it just shortens the ult cooldown outright with a massive haste number.

### Recommended pairings

#### Eureka

Eureka gives Ability Haste equal to 20% of your AP.

The more AP you have, the more Ability Haste you get, so you scale ult damage and cast frequency at the same time.

Good with:

- Rabadon's Deathcap
- Phenomenal Evil
- the Wooglet's Witchcap quest
- ADAPt

#### Infinite Recursion

Straight up 60 Ability Haste, plus a permanent 3 Ability Haste every time you get a takedown.

Karthus's ult hits all five enemies at once so assists come easy, which means your Ability Haste just keeps climbing late.

### Build adjustments

Swap one or two attack speed items into your normal AP build:

- Nashor's Tooth
- Lich Bane

Caster converts the attack speed on those items into Ability Haste.

Suggested build:

> Blackfire Torch
> + Malignance
> + Nashor's Tooth
> + Lich Bane
> + Rabadon's Deathcap
> + Shadowflame or Void Staff

If you already have enough haste, cut one attack speed item and go back to Deathcap, Shadowflame or magic pen so you're not casting ult constantly for no damage.

---

## Route 3: Tooth Fairy + Axiom Arc

This has the highest ceiling of the three and is the hardest to get going early.

What Tooth Fairy does:

> Deal more than 25% of an enemy champion's max health in damage within 2.5 seconds and they drop a tooth.

Each tooth permanently gives:

- 3 lethality
- 3 flat magic penetration

Each enemy has a 4-second cooldown on dropping teeth.

Teeth raise both Karthus's magic damage and the ult cooldown refund Axiom Arc gives on takedowns.

### Axiom Arc synergy

On a takedown, Axiom Arc refunds:

> 10% + 0.25% × lethality
> of your ult's total cooldown

In theory, at 360 lethality:

> 10% + 360 × 0.25%
> = 100%

At that point a single kill or assist fully resets your ult.

You don't actually need 360 lethality in a real game, because Karthus's ult can pick up several kills or assists at once. Every takedown triggers Axiom Arc separately, so two or three assists back to back reset the ult just the same.

### How do you stack teeth early?

Your damage is low early, so you can't just sit in the back waiting on ult.

Fast ways to proc Tooth Fairy:

1. Snowball into the enemy group.
2. Turn on E for constant AoE damage.
3. Land isolated Q's on squishies.
4. Keep dealing damage with your passive after you die.
5. Proc a tooth off each enemy individually.

Before your ult damage is online, a lone R usually can't take 25% of a target's health in 2.5 seconds, so early on you still have to walk in and stack teeth yourself.

Once your items and tooth count go up, the ult alone knocks teeth out of several enemies at once, and it snowballs faster and faster from there.

### Recommended build

Core items:

- Blackfire Torch
- Shadowflame
- Rabadon's Deathcap
- Axiom Arc
- Malignance
- Void Staff or Horizon Focus

The AD on Axiom Arc does almost nothing for Karthus, but its ult-refresh passive is the whole reason this route works.

### When to ult

Don't ult the second it comes back up.

It's better to wait for:

- at least two enemies to be low
- teammates about to finish a kill
- the ult to reliably pick up multiple assists
- no Zhonya's, spell shield or other damage negation on the enemy team

If the ult gets no kill or assist, Axiom Arc doesn't proc and the loop breaks outright.

---

## Which of the three should you pick?

### Archmage route

- Most consistent to get online
- Highest execution requirement
- Needs 234 Ability Haste
- You have to hold Q and E so the refunds go straight into W and R

### Caster route

- Easiest way to stack a ridiculous haste number
- Eureka and Infinite Recursion both fit perfectly
- You can swap some of your AP items for attack speed items
- Leans on a quirky interaction, so it's the most patch-sensitive

### Tooth Fairy route

- Weakest early and the longest ramp
- Highest late-game damage and reset ceiling
- You have to go in and stack teeth, not sit in fountain waiting on ult
- Axiom Arc only resets the ult off a kill or assist

guides.title: Kamikaze Terrain'd AP Jarvan IV
guides.summary: Playable any time you get Terrain'd. Champions without a dash get walled in and burned down.
guides.gameplay:
> Use Terrain'd to power up the damage from the terrain Jarvan's ult creates, then pair it with Imperial Mandate, Malignance and Bloodletter's Curse to keep amping damage and shredding MR. Once it's online, Jarvan stops being the traditional engage bot and becomes a burst champ who walls a squishy in and deletes them.

## How it works

Terrain'd makes terrain your champion creates deal bonus magic damage.

The two obvious users of this augment are Trundle and Jarvan, but they don't get the same value out of it:

- Trundle's pillar is a basic ability, so it only gets about 20% AP scaling.
- Jarvan's Cataclysm is an ultimate, so it gets double, roughly 40% AP scaling.

That means Jarvan's ult keeps its original physical damage and adds a chunk of magic damage that scales with AP.

The core game plan:

> EQ in and knock the enemy up
> → the ult's terrain procs Terrain'd
> → Imperial Mandate makes them Vulnerable
> → Malignance burns inside the ult zone and lowers MR
> → Shadowflame, Deathcap and Bloodletter's keep amplifying the magic damage
> → Axiom Arc resets the ult off kills and assists

With the build finished, a single Jarvan ult carries all of:

- Cataclysm's base physical damage
- Terrain'd's bonus magic damage
- Imperial Mandate's Vulnerable amp
- Malignance's zone burn
- Shadowflame's low-health amp
- Bloodletter's MR shred

Any squishy trapped inside the ult ring is very unlikely to survive all of that.

## The fixed six-item build

The final build from the video:

1. Imperial Mandate
2. Axiom Arc
3. Malignance
4. Shadowflame
5. Rabadon's Deathcap
6. Bloodletter's Curse

All six of these buff Jarvan's ult, directly or indirectly.

## Imperial Mandate

Imperial Mandate is the most cost-efficient early item in this build.

It only costs 2400 gold, yet it covers just about everything Jarvan's CC wants:

- 65 AP
- 15 base Ability Haste
- another 15 Ability Haste on crowd control abilities
- CC'ing an enemy applies Vulnerable to them for a few seconds

Imperial Mandate's effect works on both Jarvan's EQ and his ult.

That means his key abilities get around 30 Ability Haste, and anyone he CCs takes roughly 6% extra damage on top.

For AP Terrain'd Jarvan, Imperial Mandate solves AP, cooldowns and damage amp all at once, which makes it a great first item.

## Axiom Arc

Axiom Arc is mainly there to reset Jarvan's ult.

Once Jarvan walls a squishy in with his ult, kills and assists come easily, which triggers Axiom Arc's ult cooldown refund.

The AD part of the item isn't a stat this build cares about, but his ult still deals physical damage, so the AD isn't completely wasted either.

With ult haste plus takedown refunds once it's all online, the Jarvan in the video gets his ult cooldown down to around 10 seconds.

The ideal teamfight rhythm:

> The ult kills someone
> → Axiom Arc refunds cooldown
> → wait for the next EQ
> → dive in and wall another squishy

## Malignance

Malignance is the most important ult-synergy item in this build.

It gives ultimate ability haste, and after your ult damages an enemy it drops a lasting burn zone under them.

Jarvan's ult uses terrain to trap enemies in place, so Malignance's zone damage lands in full very easily.

Normally enemies can just walk out of the Malignance zone, but walled in by Jarvan's ult they usually eat several ticks of burn.

What Malignance does here:

- Cuts your ult cooldown
- Adds sustained magic damage
- Lowers enemy magic resist
- Combines with the terrain lock to land more burn ticks

Once the ult traps a target you can usually count on about three ticks of Malignance burn.

Don't drop the terrain the moment the ult lands. Keeping the walls up a bit longer keeps enemies inside the Malignance zone for longer.

## Shadowflame

Shadowflame is there to raise your burst against low-health champions.

Once Terrain'd, Malignance and the ult have pushed someone low, Shadowflame amps all your follow-up magic damage by about 20%.

It's especially good at closing out squishies:

> The first hit of the ult drops them low
> → Malignance keeps burning
> → Shadowflame amps magic damage in the low-health window
> → you finish the kill and proc Axiom Arc

Shadowflame is what turns Jarvan's ult from "chunked them" into "killed them."

## Rabadon's Deathcap

Terrain'd gives Jarvan's ult about 40% AP scaling, so Deathcap pays off very directly.

Deathcap adds roughly 30% more total AP, which boosts:

- Terrain'd's bonus magic damage
- the magic damage on Jarvan's E
- Imperial Mandate's damage
- Malignance's burn damage

Once Deathcap is done your ult burst jumps noticeably, and it's the key item for deleting squishies late.

## Bloodletter's Curse

Bloodletter's Curse gives AP, health and Ability Haste, and it keeps shredding a target's magic resist as you deal magic damage.

Jarvan's ult, Terrain'd, Malignance and his E all help stack it.

Fully stacked it strips up to about 30% magic resist, which pushes all of your magic damage higher.

Its synergy with Malignance is the key part:

> Malignance keeps ticking magic damage
> → Bloodletter's stacks fast
> → their magic resist keeps dropping
> → Terrain'd and the ongoing burn hit harder and harder

The health it gives also takes a little of the edge off how squishy Jarvan is after he dives in.

## Playing it out

### Before the fight

This Jarvan isn't the guy who mindlessly engages into all five of them.

Before a fight, use E and EQ to feel out enemy positioning and look for:

- ADCs with no dash
- mages standing too far up
- targets who already used Flash or their escape
- spots where several enemies are stacked together

If all you can wall in is their tank, the whole burst loses most of its value.

## Good games for it

This build works best when:

- the enemy team has a lot of squishies
- the enemy champions lack dashes
- the enemy tends to group up tightly
- your team has another frontline
- Jarvan can get kills or assists consistently
- the game can go long enough to finish several AP items
- the enemy isn't stacking magic resist items

Against dashless ADCs and mages, all Jarvan has to do is land his ult and he gets the full Terrain'd and Malignance package every time.

## Bad games for it

It's rough in these situations:

- the enemy has a lot of tanks and high-MR champions
- the enemy has tons of dashes, Flashes or wall-hopping
- Jarvan is your team's only frontline
- Jarvan has to be the one soaking damage up front
- the enemy has a lot of shields, invulnerability or untargetability
- you can't get early kills, so Axiom Arc has nothing to work with
- it's hard to reach the enemy backline in fights

This build has very few defensive stats. If Jarvan dives in and doesn't kill his target fast, he tends to just die in the middle of their team.

## Other augments worth taking

### Silver augments

- ADAPt
- Forged By The Master
- Dive Bomber

ADAPt pushes the AP build even further, and Dive Bomber suits a champ like Jarvan who has a hard time getting out safely after diving in.

### Gold augments

- Combusting Interest
- Shrink Engine
- Shark Tempest

Prioritize anything that adds damage, ability frequency or dive burst.

### Prismatic augments

- Infinite Recursion
- DropBear
- Surge Field

Infinite Recursion keeps cutting your ult cooldown further.

DropBear and other on-death augments are also perfect for Jarvan, because his ult is already a one-way trip. Even if he dies after diving in, the death effect keeps adding damage and helping the team pick up kills.

## Things to watch out for

- The bonus damage from Terrain'd is magic damage, so AP, magic pen and MR shred all matter a lot.
- Jarvan's ult still deals its original physical damage, so the burst is mixed damage.
- The Imperial Mandate interaction with EQ and the ult was tested on the video's patch and could get changed later.
- Don't drop the walls right after the ult traps someone, or you'll land fewer ticks of Malignance burn.
- Axiom Arc only refunds ult cooldown if you get a kill or assist.
- An ult roughly every 10 seconds is the ideal case, with the full build and the takedown loop running.
- This isn't tank Jarvan; dive the wrong target and you evaporate.
- Go for squishies, and don't dump all your abilities into a high-MR frontliner.
- Augment and item effects can change with patches, so trust the current in-game text.

guides.title: Fan The Hammer AP Gnar
guides.summary: Gnar's W third-hit proc has a 100% AP ratio and his ultimate has 150%, so you stack AP items and let the passive do the damage. Worth trying for fun when the enemy team has a lot of squishies — one auto can burst someone down.
guides.gameplay:
## Core Mechanic

When Fan The Hammer hits an enemy champion, it fires 5 extra arrows.

So a single auto attack is really:

> 1 hit from the auto itself
> ＋ 5 hits from the extra arrows
> ＝ 6 separate attack instances

Mini Gnar's W procs its third-hit bonus every 3 attacks or damaging abilities.

So under this special interaction:

> The first 3 instances trigger one W
> ＋ the next 3 instances trigger another W
> ＝ one auto attack triggers two third-hit procs

At max rank, a single W proc has a huge AP ratio and also deals magic damage based on the target's max health. Stack two procs together and you put out enormous burst on squishies and high-health frontliners alike.

This build relies on a special on-hit interaction, so once you pick up the augment, test in a real fight whether one auto really does trigger two Ws.

## Core Augments

### Fan The Hammer

Absolutely mandatory.

Without Fan The Hammer, Mini Gnar has to land three normal attacks for one W proc, so you never get the double-proc burst.

### Recommended Pairings

- **Dual Wield**: more extra attacks and more on-hit procs
- **Scopier Weapons**: extra attack range, which makes that first auto much safer
- **Jeweled Gauntlet**: raises the ceiling on your ability magic damage
- **Giant Slayer**: more damage against high-health champions
- **Ethereal Weapon**: brings more of your abilities into the on-hit system


## Rage Management

Mini Gnar's W is your main damage source, and you lose the third-hit proc completely once you turn into Mega Gnar.

Before a fight, remember to:

- Not sit there auto attacking minions
- Keep your Rage as low as you can
- Not force autos when you're about to transform
- Focus on E, R, and W crowd control once you're Mega Gnar
- Look for the double-proc burst again after you revert to Mini Gnar

The rhythm of this build is:

> Mini Gnar handles the one-auto burst
> Mega Gnar handles the engage and crowd control

## Good Matchups

This works well when:

- The enemy team is short-ranged or stacked with frontline
- Your team has a solid frontline to protect you
- The enemy doesn't have much magic resist
- Gnar can safely get into auto attack range
- You get Fan The Hammer early in the first round

It's weaker when:

- The enemy team is all ultra-long-range champions
- The enemy has a ton of point-and-click crowd control
- Your team has no frontline at all
- The enemy stacks heavy magic resist early
- You can't keep your Rage under control before fights

## Things to Watch For

- Fan The Hammer only triggers when you attack enemy champions.
- One auto attack theoretically creates 6 attack instances and triggers two W procs.
- Your main damage comes from W, not from the arrows themselves.
- W is magic damage, so AP and magic penetration matter a lot.
- You have to manage Rage before a fight so you don't transform into Mega Gnar too early.
- Full AP Mini Gnar is extremely squishy, so pull back the instant you land that first auto.
- The special W interaction may get changed in a patch, so test in game whether you still get two procs.

## Summary

The core combo is:

> Fan The Hammer adds 5 extra arrows
> ＋ your own auto makes 6 attack instances
> ＋ Mini Gnar's W procs every 3 instances
> ＝ one auto attack triggers two W procs

Add AP, magic pen, and attack range on top of that, and you end up with:

> Q to slow
> → auto for the double proc
> → W to speed away
> → wait for the next burst window
>

guides.title: Fan The Hammer Sion: The 60% Max Health Zombie Punch Build
guides.summary: Sion's passive deals 10% of the target's max health on every auto attack, and Fan The Hammer triggers it 5 extra times, so one auto takes 60% of their health bar.
guides.gameplay:
## Core of the Build

The absolute core of this build:

- ![augment:Fan The Hammer](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1220.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- **Sion's passive: Glory in Death**

Fan The Hammer does this:

> When you attack an enemy champion, fire 5 extra arrows.

Every arrow deals physical damage and can:

- Crit independently
- Trigger on-hit effects
- Trigger some champion passives
- Track its cooldown separately per attack direction

Once Sion dies and enters zombie form, his auto attacks gain:

- Massive attack speed
- 100% lifesteal
- Bonus physical damage equal to 10% of the target's max health

With the current interaction, Fan The Hammer's 5 arrows also trigger that max health damage.

So one attack theoretically produces:

> The auto itself: 10% of the target's max health
> ＋ 5 extra arrows: 5 × 10% of the target's max health
> ＝ 60% of the target's max health as physical damage

Add the auto attack, the arrows' own damage, crits, and item on-hit effects on top, and the real total from one auto is even higher.

Why Does It Only Work After You Die?
------------------------

While Sion is alive, his auto attacks don't carry the passive's 10% max health damage.

While he's alive, Fan The Hammer mostly just gives you:

- 5 extra arrows
- Extra physical damage
- Item on-hit procs
- Crit rolls

The absurd 60% max health interaction only shows up once Sion enters zombie form.

The whole build splits into two phases:

### While Alive

Your job is to:

- Engage with Q and R
- Stack bonus health with W
- Soak up the enemy's crowd control and damage
- Get as close to the enemy backline as possible
- Set up a good damage position for zombie form

### After You Die

Now your job becomes:

> Pop the zombie form's speed rush
> → close on an enemy champion
> → land that first Fan The Hammer auto
> → keep auto attacking with the huge attack speed
> → chase down the next target

Sion is the frontline while he's alive; he only becomes the real burst carry after he dies.

---

## Core Items

The two most important items for this build:

1. **Titanic Hydra**
2. **Overlord's Bloodmail**

After that, go crit, armor pen, or defensive items depending on the game.

---

## Titanic Hydra

Titanic Hydra fits Sion perfectly.

Its autos add bonus physical damage scaling off your own max health, and Sion keeps gaining bonus health from his W passive.

The stat chain looks like this:

> W passive stacks health
> → Titanic Hydra's on-hit damage goes up
> → Fan The Hammer's arrows trigger some of those on-hit effects
> → one auto carries several chunks of extra damage

The item also improves Sion's wave clear and close-range damage while he's alive.

In zombie form Sion has enormous attack speed, so he procs Titanic Hydra's on-hit over and over.

---

## Overlord's Bloodmail

Overlord's Bloodmail converts bonus health into attack damage.

Sion can pick up a lot of bonus health from:

- W passive stacks off last hits and champion kills
- Heartsteel
- Tank Engine
- Steel Your Heart
- Health items
- Stat-boosting augments

Run all of that health through Overlord's Bloodmail and it turns into a mountain of AD.

The full chain:

> Stack health
> → Sion is tankier while alive
> → Titanic Hydra hits harder
> → Overlord's Bloodmail hands you a pile of attack damage
> → zombie form autos and Fan The Hammer arrows hit harder

Once Sion goes zombie his health decays constantly, so he drops to low health quickly and gets Overlord's Bloodmail's low-health AD value that much faster.


## Things to Watch For

- Fan The Hammer only triggers on enemy champions, never on minions.
- The 60% max health interaction only exists in Sion's zombie form.
- Don't auto attack while alive, or you'll waste Fan The Hammer's charge
- Sion can't proc the passive's 10% max health damage while he's alive.
- The bonus max health damage is physical, so armor reduces it.
- Titanic Hydra and Overlord's Bloodmail are the two items that fit the health-stacking system best.
- Full crit does the most damage, but the bruiser route is more consistent.
- Scopier Weapons noticeably fixes zombie Sion's problem of never being able to reach anyone.
- That first auto attack matters far more than trying to stand and trade.

## Summary

Fan The Hammer Sion isn't about dealing damage while alive — it's about using zombie form for the burst:

> Sion's passive adds 10% of the target's max health to every attack
> ＋ Fan The Hammer fires 5 extra arrows
> ＋ the special interaction lets those arrows re-trigger the passive
> → one auto theoretically deals 60% of the target's max health as physical damage

Then stack on:

> Titanic Hydra turning health into on-hit damage
> ＋ Overlord's Bloodmail turning bonus health into attack damage
> ＋ crit and percentage armor pen amplifying the real numbers

and you end up with a zombie burst build that engages and soaks damage while alive, then kills people with one or two autos after it dies.

guides.title: Infernal Conduit Statikk Shiv Fizz: The Infinite E AoE Burn Build
guides.summary: Use Statikk Shiv's on-hit to spread Fizz's W bleed, then let the bleed trigger Infernal Conduit's burn to cut the cooldowns on Q, W, and E.
guides.gameplay:
## Core of the Build

The core combination for this build:

- ![augment:Infernal Conduit](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1045.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![item:Statikk Shiv](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223087.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![item:Liandry's Torment](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/6653.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)
- ![item:Blackfire Torch](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/222503.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The full chain:

> Turn on W
> → use Q or an auto to proc Statikk Shiv
> → the Shiv bounces onto several enemy champions
> → the secondary targets also take Fizz's W on-hit
> → multiple enemies end up bleeding from W
> → Liandry's and Blackfire Torch pile on more burn
> → all that burn keeps triggering Infernal Conduit
> → Q, W, and E cooldowns get slashed
> → cast E, Q, and W again

The more enemies there are and the tighter they group up, the more times Infernal Conduit triggers.

That means this build can feel close to infinite abilities when all five of them are stacked together, but the refresh rate drops off noticeably in a 1v1 or against a spread-out team.

---

## Why Does This Work on Fizz?

Fizz's W has two separate parts.

### W Passive

Fizz's auto attacks apply magic damage that ticks over several seconds.

That counts as damage over time, so it triggers Infernal Conduit's cooldown reduction.

Normally, one auto attack only applies W to a single target.

With the reworked Statikk Shiv:

> An auto or Q procs the Shiv
> → the Shiv bounces to nearby enemies
> → the bounce targets also take the W on-hit
> → one attack applies the W bleed to several enemies at once

That effectively turns Fizz's single-target damage over time into AoE damage over time.

### W Active

When you activate W, Fizz's next attack gains bonus magic damage, and his autos keep dealing bonus damage for a while afterward.

When the Shiv procs, the secondary targets don't just get the W passive bleed — they also eat the W-related on-hit.

So the most reliable opener is:

> W first, then Q

rather than jumping in with a raw Q.

---

## How Does Infernal Conduit Refresh Abilities?

Infernal Conduit's key effect:

> Every time your burn damage hits an enemy champion, all of your basic ability cooldowns are reduced by 0.08 seconds.

It only refreshes basic abilities:

- Q gets refreshed
- W gets refreshed
- E gets refreshed
- R is not refreshed directly by Infernal Conduit

One Shiv bounce puts Fizz's W bleed on several targets, and with Liandry's and Blackfire Torch layered on top, every enemy has multiple damage-over-time effects running at once.

Hit several enemies and you'll have all of these going at the same time:

- Fizz's W damage over time
- Infernal Conduit's own burn
- Liandry's burn
- Blackfire Torch burn

All of those keep ticking on multiple champions.

Every tick can trigger Infernal Conduit, so a teamfight generates a huge number of cooldown reduction procs in a very short time.

That's exactly why Fizz can chain E after E.

---

## The Core Three Items

### 1.  ![item:Statikk Shiv](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/223087.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The Shiv is what starts the whole engine.

Without it, Fizz's W usually only lands on a single target, so Infernal Conduit barely triggers.

With the Shiv:

> One attack
> → bounces to multiple targets
> → all of them get W applied
> → Infernal Conduit triggers off the whole group

You're not building the Shiv for its own lightning damage — you're building it to spread the W on-hit across their entire team.

So even though some of the physical stats it gives are wasted on a traditional AP Fizz, it's still the irreplaceable core item for this build.

### 2.  ![item:Liandry's Torment](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/6653.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Liandry's is there to add a second layer of burn.

Once Fizz's W is on a target, Liandry's keeps dealing magic damage over time.

What it gives you:

- More Infernal Conduit procs
- More damage against high-health champions
- Longer damage-over-time duration on enemies
- Ability refreshes that keep going even after enemies leave the fight

Liandry's scales especially well when the enemy has a lot of frontline.

### 3.  ![item:Blackfire Torch](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/222503.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Blackfire Torch provides AP, mana, and Ability Haste, plus another item burn.

This item solves three problems:

- The mana strain from casting abilities constantly
- Not having enough baseline Ability Haste early
- Infernal Conduit needing more burn sources

Once the Shiv has spread W to several enemies, the Torch widens both your damage over time and your refresh rate.

The core three items in one line:

> The Shiv spreads W
> ＋ Liandry's adds burn
> ＋ Blackfire Torch adds burn and mana
> ＋ Infernal Conduit turns burn into ability cooldown

## Other Augment Pairings

### ![augment:Mystic Punch](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1058.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The reworked Shiv carries on-hit effects to multiple targets, and Mystic Punch cuts a flat amount off your cooldowns whenever an on-hit lands.

When the Shiv hits several enemies at once, you can trigger Mystic Punch several times in a row.

That's an instant burst of cooldown refund on top of Infernal Conduit's continuous reduction.

Once you have it, your ability refreshes get much more consistent.

### ![augment:Ethereal Weapon](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1029.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Ethereal Weapon makes your abilities apply on-hit effects.

Fizz's Q already triggers on-hit by itself, but Ethereal Weapon brings his other abilities into the Shiv and W system too.

Note that the old "Ethereal Weapon procs Fizz's W infinitely" loop from previous patches has been fixed.

You take Ethereal Weapon now for the extra ways to trigger on-hit effects, not for the old infinite W exploit.

###  ![augment:Vulnerability](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1092.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Vulnerability lets item damage and damage over time crit.

This build runs a ton of item burn, so with Vulnerability the Torch, Liandry's, the Shiv, and your other item damage all get a much higher ceiling.

Vulnerability raises your damage; it doesn't directly increase how often Infernal Conduit triggers.

### Ability Haste Augments

Options include:

- Eureka
- Infinite Recursion
- Recursion
- Shrink Engine
- E-specific ability haste
- Generic Ability Haste stats

These lower the number of burn ticks the infinite loop needs.

The shorter your base cooldowns, the easier it is for Infernal Conduit to wipe out what's left

## What Beats This Build?

### Point-and-Click Crowd Control

Fizz is untargetable during E, but he can still get locked down after he lands.

Enemies can read your landing spot and use a stun, silence, fear, or suppression to cut off your next E.

### Enemies Spreading Out

When the Shiv can't bounce between multiple enemy champions, your W and burn coverage isn't wide enough and your abilities won't come back instantly.

### Magic Resist Items

Almost all of this build's damage is magic.

Once the enemy picks up Force of Nature, Spirit Visage, or heavy magic resist, you need to add Void Staff as soon as possible.

### Running Out of Mana

Spamming Q, W, and E burns through your mana fast.

Blackfire Torch matters a lot here — don't just build Shiv and Liandry's and then stack pure AP.

## Summary

Infernal Conduit Fizz isn't about simply stacking Ability Haste — it's about using the Shiv to generate a mass of AoE burn procs:

> W provides damage over time
> ＋ the Shiv spreads W to multiple champions
> ＋ Liandry's and the Torch add more burn sources
> ＋ Infernal Conduit turns every burn tick into basic ability cooldown
> → Q, W, and E refresh at high speed
> → Fizz keeps using E to go untargetable

Once it's fully online, as long as several enemies are inside the Shiv's bounce range, Fizz can loop this over and over:

> W then Q to engage
> → the Shiv applies W to the group
> → E to dodge damage
> → the burn refreshes your abilities
> → E again

The end result is constant dashes, AoE burn, and something very close to a permanent E.

guides.title: Goliath Pyke
guides.summary: Abuse Pyke's passive that converts bonus health into attack damage: pair Goliath with health items to build absurd AD and a massive ultimate execute threshold.
guides.gameplay:
## How It Works

Pyke can't gain bonus max health from items the normal way.

Whenever Pyke does gain bonus health, his passive converts it into bonus attack damage. So health, a defensive stat on every other champion, becomes an offensive stat on Pyke.

![augment:Goliath](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1041.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1) gives you all of the following at once:

- Percentage max health
- Adaptive Force
- A larger champion model

The percent health gets converted into attack damage by Pyke's passive, and the Adaptive Force adds even more attack damage on top, so you're getting paid twice.

The goal of this build isn't to turn Pyke into a tank — it's to use health items to build absurd amounts of attack damage.

## Recommended Build

#### ![item:Hubris](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/226697.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Your first core item.

Pyke chains kills and assists with his ultimate, which stacks Hubris' growth effect quickly. By the mid to late game, Hubris alone provides a huge amount of attack damage.

This item sets the ceiling on the whole build, and the earlier you finish it the easier it is to stack.

#### ![item:Axiom Arc](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/226696.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Provides attack damage, lethality, and ultimate-related value.

Pyke's most important cleanup tool is his ultimate, and Axiom Arc gets it back faster so he can keep hunting for executes in a teamfight.

#### ![item:Warmog's Armor](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/items/443083.png?imageView2/1/w/64/h/64/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Warmog's provides a mountain of health.

Pyke never actually keeps that bonus health — he converts it into attack damage. So in this build the item's main value isn't tankiness, it's a giant pile of AD.

## Playing the Game

### Early Game

Play the early game like a normal Pyke. Don't dive straight into a group of them just because you picked up Goliath.

Your priorities:

- Look for hook opportunities with Q
- Follow up with E for extra crowd control
- Finish Hubris as fast as possible
- Stack Hubris with kills and assists
- Make sure you aren't dying over and over

This build leans hard on items and stacks, so a string of early deaths badly slows down your spike.

### Mid Game

Once Hubris and Axiom Arc are done, start hunting low-health enemies for cleanup kills.

Recommended sequence:

1. Use W to approach from the side while invisible.
2. Use Q or E to help your team lock someone down.
3. Wait until the enemy is inside your ultimate's execute threshold, then use it.
4. Immediately look for the next low-health target after the kill.
5. Back off when there's no execute available — don't stand in the middle of them auto attacking.

Even though Pyke buys several health items, that bonus health has already been converted into attack damage, so his actual body is still paper.

### Late Game

With the build finished, Pyke's attack damage on the stat sheet is enormous.

That doesn't just raise your ultimate's execute threshold — it also boosts your auto attacks, Q, and E. Against squishy champions you often don't even need a full combo to push them into execute range.

Don't be the first one in from the front in a teamfight. The right order is:

1. Let your team engage first.
2. Use W to come in from the side.
3. Lock down a key target with Q or E.
4. Weave in your empowered auto attacks.
5. Land your first execute with your ultimate.
6. Use the reset to keep cleaning up.

## When to Pick This

This build is a good fit when:

- The enemy team has a lot of squishy champions
- Your team has another frontline champion
- Your team has reliable crowd control
- Pyke can pick up kills and assists easily
- The game is likely to reach the mid to late game

## When Not to Pick This

Don't force it in these situations:

- The enemy team has a lot of tanks
- You didn't get Goliath

## Things to Watch For

### Goliath Does Not Make Pyke Tanky

The bonus health gets converted into attack damage, so Pyke's real health pool doesn't grow with items the way it normally would.

guides.title: Infinite Q Master Yi with Mystic Punch: Full Guide
guides.summary: Mystic Punch plus 130 Ability Haste is all you need to pull it off
guides.gameplay:
> Built entirely around Mystic Punch: Master Yi's Q lands multiple attack instances, and each one cuts your cooldowns. Once Q's real cooldown is pushed under about 7.5 seconds, you can recast it the moment you land, which keeps you untargetable for long stretches.

## How It Works

Mystic Punch does this:

> When an on-hit effect lands, all of your ability cooldowns are reduced by a flat 1.25 seconds.

Master Yi's Q, Alpha Strike, is a multi-hit ability, and in the current ARAM Mayhem patch those multiple damage instances trigger Mystic Punch back to back.

One full Q plus a follow-up auto attack shaves off roughly 7.5 seconds of cooldown in total.

So as long as you push Q's real cooldown under 7.5 seconds, you get:

> Q to go untargetable
> → the multi-hit damage triggers Mystic Punch
> → land and add one auto attack
> → Q's cooldown is wiped completely
> → cast Q again immediately

## Core Augments

### ![augment:Mystic Punch](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1058.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

The irreplaceable core of the entire build.

Without Mystic Punch, Master Yi can still lower Q's cooldown with auto attacks, but chaining Qs back to back is basically impossible.

If you see Mystic Punch, you can lock in the infinite Q build right there.

### ![augment:Bread And Butter](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1103.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives a big chunk of Q-specific ability haste, making it the most direct secondary core.

With it, Q easily reaches the cooldown threshold the infinite loop needs, which frees up item slots for damage and survivability.

### ![augment:Dashing](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1019.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Master Yi's Q counts as a dash, so it gets a very large amount of ability-specific haste.

It doesn't just help the infinite Q come online — it also shortens Q's dead time when Mystic Punch hasn't fully triggered yet.

### ![augment:Recursion](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1068.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Straight-up Ability Haste, simple and reliable.

If you already have Mystic Punch but your item haste is still short, Recursion is a perfect supplement.

### ![augment:Infinite Recursion](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/1388.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Gives Ability Haste up front and keeps growing as you pick up takedowns.

Master Yi cleans up teamfights easily, so your haste keeps climbing into the late game.

### ![augment:Purist - Caster](https://www.cchappy.top/hks/assets/hextech-aram/augments/latest/2018.png?imageView2/1/w/96/h/96/format/webp/q/75/ignore-error/1)

Converts attack speed into Ability Haste.

Master Yi wants a lot of attack speed anyway and his ultimate grants more, so this covers both auto attack frequency and Q's cooldown at once.

This route does lean more on the right item and augment combination, though, so it's less consistent than Bread And Butter or Dashing.

## Recommended Build

The build for infinite Q Master Yi has three jobs:

1. Provide enough Ability Haste
2. Solve the mana cost of casting Q constantly
3. Make sure you don't get locked down or bursted the instant Q ends

Recommended items:

1. Hubris
2. Essence Reaver
3. Spear of Shojin
4. Black Cleaver
5. Death's Dance
6. Endless Hunger

The build isn't completely fixed — adjust it based on how much Ability Haste you've already picked up.

### Essence Reaver

One of the most important utility items in this build.

Spamming Q drains mana fast. Without mana sustain you can meet the cooldown requirement and still be unable to cast because you're dry.

Essence Reaver gives you:

- Attack damage
- Crit
- Ability Haste
- Mana back on auto attacks

Master Yi has to add an auto attack every time he lands from Q anyway, so the mana refund triggers easily.

### Spear of Shojin

Provides a lot of basic ability haste, which visibly cuts Q's listed cooldown.

Master Yi casts Q, W, and E constantly, so he also gets good mileage out of the item's ramping damage.

If you didn't get a Q-specific haste augment, Spear of Shojin is a high priority.

### Black Cleaver

Provides attack damage, health, and Ability Haste.

Q's multiple damage instances stack the armor shred quickly. Against several fighters or a real frontline, Cleaver improves both your survivability and your sustained damage.

### Death's Dance

Infinite Q doesn't mean you're actually invincible.

Master Yi touches down briefly at the end of every Q, and if he gets locked down or focused there, he can still die on the spot.

Death's Dance spreads out burst damage and heals you on takedowns, which suits chaining kills in teamfights.

### Hubris

Good in games where you can reliably pick up early kills.

Once Master Yi is online he chains cleanup kills easily, and Hubris keeps adding attack damage, boosting both Q and your auto attacks.

If the early game goes badly and you can't stack Hubris reliably, prioritize steadier haste or survivability items instead.

### Endless Hunger

Provides attack damage and extra basic ability cooldown reduction, which makes the Q loop even more consistent.

If your augments already gave you enough Ability Haste, you can swap it for another damage or defensive item.

## Adjusting the Build

### Not Enough Haste

Prioritize:

- Spear of Shojin
- Black Cleaver
- Death's Dance
- Other high Ability Haste items

The goal is to push Q's listed cooldown under 7.5 seconds.

### Haste Already Covered

You can cut one pure haste item and add:

- Infinity Edge
- The Collector
- Blade of the Ruined King
- Maw of Malmortius
- Mercurial Scimitar

Don't keep mindlessly stacking haste once you've met the infinite Q requirement, or you'll run into a damage problem.

### Enemy Has a Lot of Crowd Control

Prioritize:

- Mercury's Treads
- Mercurial Scimitar
- Maw of Malmortius
- Death's Dance
- Tenacity augments

What infinite Q Master Yi fears isn't heavy damage — it's getting locked down the instant he lands.

## Summary

The core formula for infinite Q Master Yi:

> Mystic Punch
> ＋ Q's multiple attack instances
> ＋ one auto attack on landing
> ＋ Q's real cooldown pushed under about 7.5 seconds
> ＋ Essence Reaver to solve mana
> ＋ survivability items so you don't get deleted on landing

Once it's online, Master Yi just repeats:

> Q → land, auto → Q → land, auto

which keeps him untargetable for long stretches and lets him chain cleanup kills inside the enemy formation.

notes.en: Good for slugfests, or when the enemy team is all tanks. Once it's online in the late game, a single W is a guaranteed execute.
Good when you roll tank augments early: Pressure Cooker, Steel Your Heart, Icathia's Fall.
There are a lot of healing augments now, like Rejuvenation and Ravenous Bind. If you don't get any of them, you can go Rod of Ages first and swap Ardent Censer for Warmog's Armor.

Small trick: with Final Form or Ultimate Awakening, cast R and then interrupt it yourself (press B to recall) or let an enemy interrupt you. R refunds its cooldown but you still get the Final Form buff.

Requirements for infinite R: Archmage + rank 4 E + 230 ability haste
The build above gives 100 ability haste; Shrink Engine, Warlock Juicebox, Eureka, Infinite Recursion, and Ultimate Awakening all get you the rest
Don't max E to rank 5, or E and R won't refresh each other
Critical Healing seems to have been removed from the pool, I've never been offered it.

Trundle rolls Terrain'd very often, and it makes E deal damage
If neither augment at level 7 is Terrain'd, go the support build
Three augments for infinite E: Infernal Conduit; Archmage (W and E refresh each other); Warlock Juicebox with Lich Bane + Nashor's Tooth, no autos needed for the passive
Only Rhaast (red Kayn) exists in ARAM. Don't be afraid to die in the first 5 minutes, collect orbs and transform early.
Take AD or attack speed on your stat shards, E benefits from both. Don't take Lil' Extra Help, E gets nothing from it.
With Master of Duality against a tanky enemy team, you can build a few extra tank items, stack AP endlessly, and squishies die the moment you look at them.
Good when the enemy has a lot of divers or assassins. Super obnoxious.
Varus has a lot of viable styles: go the poke build against squishy teams, and AP or the on-hit build when they're tanky.
Don't take Draw Your Sword.
The lethality build is good if you get Draw Your Sword or Blade Waltz early.
Poke with Q, and use E to slow or root the enemy.
Vayne's augment pool is very clean this patch, just go the crit build unless the enemy team is tanky.
Trick: if Jayce rolls an omnivamp stat shard, make sure to switch to hammer form before taking it for 10% more omnivamp.
Trick: at level 6 don't put a point in anything, check whether Scopier Weapons shows up at level 7. Take it first, then level up, and it'll be calculated with melee scaling.
Warlock Juicebox is bugged right now: ulting in your post-death spirit form takes 40 seconds off R's cooldown. For items you can build Nashor's Tooth + Lich Bane.

Three routes to infinite R
1. Archmage: refresh R with W, you need 234+ haste
2. Warlock Juicebox: 300+ haste, paired with Eureka or Infinite Recursion. Roughly one ult every 10 seconds, and it's the easiest to pull off
3. Tooth Fairy: once you have enough stacks, any ult that picks up an assist gives you infinite ults
No fixed augments, pick based on the enemy comp, mainly ability haste and move speed. You have to keep yourself alive to be annoying, and you only deal damage if you're alive!!!
Landing Q decides your follow-up damage: stack marks with Q, then dive in with E to finish them off, and turn on W for the speed before you engage.
Prioritize omnivamp and move speed augments. Gwen should deal with the frontline first and use W to avoid damage and abilities from the backline.
Heavily debuffed, damage is very low. Stack haste for wave clear and build utility items.

With Purist, max W and infinite W is easy to pull off. You just need 345 haste (Eureka or Infinite Recursion), prioritize haste on your stat shards, then build AP attack speed items and you're online. If you don't get it, just play the normal AP build; tank isn't really recommended.

Infinite W is actually pretty hard, there are three routes:
1. Archmage: stack 200+ haste, then refresh W and E off each other
2. Infernal Conduit: 160+ haste, and W has to hit two champions; much easier if you also have Warlock Juicebox
3. Warlock Juicebox only: 340+ haste, very hard to get online, a bit easier with Eureka or Infinite Recursion
With Tooth Fairy, Giant Slayer, or High Roller you can consider the full damage build. Critical Healing has been removed from the pool.
Good in slugfests and when the enemy has a big frontline. If they have a lot of poke, just go the full damage build.
Archmage + Warlock Juicebox + 200 haste lets you cast W and R endlessly.
The mainstream playstyle is the fixed double tear build with Mind to Matter + ADAPt. It works on Kassadin just as well as it does on Ryze.
If you roll Goliath early you can build tank; if it comes later, just play normally. With Celestial Body and Mad Scientist, the health converts into AD.
Don't take Warlock Juicebox.
Infinite shrooms: Archmage + Warlock Juicebox, with W and R refreshing each other. Items: Malignance, Nashor's Tooth, Lich Bane, Morellonomicon, Shadowflame, Cryptbloom.
Build both burn items when the enemy has a big frontline.
Fiddlesticks gets really strong once you learn to W-flash.
If you get Ethereal Weapon or Tooth Fairy early, or the enemy team is all poke champs, you can play AP; otherwise just play tank.
